She outlines how Republicans plan to address inflation, lower consumer costs and shape their legislative platform ahead of the crucial November midterm elections.
Senate Republicans racing to keep their grip on power have beef with President Donald Trump’s latest affordability push.

A handful of Republicans in the upper chamber aren’t happy with Trump’s directive to allow hundreds of thousands of tons of foreign beef into the U.S. in a bid to lower grocery bills. It comes as Americans’ struggles with everyday affordability have erupted as a key issue for voters across the country.
Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., who is up for re-election this cycle and is one of Trump’s top allies in the Senate, argued that beef prices are high "for a simple reason: Our cattle herd is too small."
TRUMP URGED TO STOP TARGETING FELLOW REPUBLICANS AS GOP FIGHTS TO KEEP MAJORITY

President Donald Trump wants to flood the market with hundreds of thousands of metric tons of foreign ground beef to lower grocery costs, but Republicans running in key races warn that the move hurts American ranchers. (Ronaldo Schemidt/AFP via Getty Images)

"Imported beef below market prices will only put more pressure on our cattlemen," Cotton said on X. "I have advised the President against this ill-advised action in the past and I now urge him to reconsider. We need to support our cattlemen, grow the herd, and let the market work."

Trump last week announced on Truth Social his intent to flood the market with 300,000 metric tons of imported ground beef with a commitment that the product would be sold at 25% below current market prices over a 90-day span.

It comes as ground beef prices have soared to roughly $7 per pound, while the nation’s cattle herd earlier this year hit historic lows not seen since the 1950s, according to data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA).
TOP GOP GROUP PUMPS $37M INTO FIGHT ON KEY ISSUE DOMINATING MIDTERM RACES: 'MUCH MORE TO COME'
Trump defended his import plan as he headed to South Carolina to stump for Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., arguing "that’s what the people want."

"That’s what the voters want, and that’s what I want. The ranchers are great. They’re my people. I love the ranchers," Trump said. "They’ve done a fantastic job, but they admit that we need a little help in order to get the prices down, so that’s what we’re doing."

Neither Trump, nor the administration, has so far said which countries the ground beef would come from. But earlier this year, he signed an executive order similarly aimed at lowering beef prices by allowing an influx of 80,000 metric tons of beef trimmings from Argentina.
Republicans at the time privately fumed over the directive in a closed-door meeting in the Senate with Vice President JD Vance.
And now, Republicans running for office in America’s heartland again disagree.
"I want to lower prices, but this is a bad idea," Rep. Ashley Hinson, R-Iowa, said on X.
SENATE MAP TIGHTENS AS TOP FORECASTER MOVES 3 RACES TOWARD DEMOCRATS
Republican candidate for the Senate Ashley Hinson speaks during a campaign event on June 1, 2026, in Dubuque, Iowa. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)
Hinson is running in one of the tightest races in the country to replace retiring Sen. Joni Ernst, R-Iowa. Cook Political Report rated the race a toss-up last week.

Other in-cycle incumbents aren’t thrilled with Trump’s push, either. Sen. Mike Rounds, R-S.D., charged, "This Hurts!," while Sen. Pete Ricketts, R-Neb., contended that he appreciated the work to "lower grocery prices," but warned that "short-term policy shifts do not equal long-term solutions."
"Flooding the market with lower quality beef compromises Nebraska farmers and ranchers," Ricketts said.
Trump’s other key Senate allies aren’t thrilled with the plan either.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Sen. Tim Sheehy, R-Mont., said he’s advised Trump not to do this for the last year because it would harm American ranchers, "most of whom are MAGA Republicans."

"The president’s heart is in the right place on wanting lower prices for the American people, and beef prices have been impacted by the Mexican screwworm," Sheehy said.The White House and the USDA did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: Socialists ripped over kids-focused push in deep-red state: ‘Next generation of comrades’
summary: Democratic Socialists of America's Charleston chapter offers childcare training to grow "budding comrades," sparking indoctrination accusations.
story: Former Missouri congressional candidate Hartzell Gray explains why he believes his socialist platform represents the future of the Democratic Party as DSA-backed candidates pick up seats.

Conservatives are blasting the Charleston, South Carolina, chapter of Democratic Socialists of America after the group shared a Facebook ad seeking volunteers to provide child care at meetings and help support its "next generation of comrades."

"No experience with kids needed! Come ready to learn how to grow and support our next generation of comrades," DSA Charleston posted to its Facebook page Friday. "If you'd like to help support our next generation of comrades, join this training to review best practices, roleplay through scenarios, and get you feeling confident to welcome and care for our budding comrades."
The group is offering the virtual Zoom training Monday evening to adults with or without children.

The training comes as DSA’s influence within Democratic politics is growing, with socialist candidates notching primary wins as the midterm campaign intensifies and giving the organization a broader platform for its policies and organizing.
DEMOCRATS LURE ‘POLITICALLY HOMELESS’ GEN Z TOWARD SOCIALISM — A COUNTERATTACK IS TAKING SHAPE
New York City Democratic mayoral nominee Zohran Mamdani delivers remarks in the Bronx, New York City, on Friday, Oct. 24, 2025. (Fox News Digital/Deirdre Heavey)
Critics accused the group of using "indoctrination" tactics, arguing the training reflects a broader push by socialists to court children.
"DSA childhood training for future 'comrades' in SOUTH CAROLINA! These people must be investigated," South Carolina Freedom Caucus founding chairman Adam Morgan wrote.
"They’re indoctrinating them as much as possible and it’s disgusting," said another user.

"They used to tell us socialism was just a Republican talking point. Now they’re advertising meetings for their ‘comrades.’ Socialism isn’t coming to South Carolina — it’s already here. And we CANNOT afford to ignore it. Far-left socialist groups are organizing in our communities and targeting the next generation with their radical agenda," wrote the South Carolina Republican Party account.
South Carolina is solid Republican territory, with President Donald Trump carrying the state by nearly 18 points in 2024 after Republicans won it in every presidential election dating back to 1980.
INSIDE TEACHERS' UNION MAY DAY 'DRESS REHEARSAL' CRITICS WARN WILL 'GROOM' STUDENTS INTO DEM 'FOOT SOLDIERS'

On Inauguration Day on Jan. 20, 2025, Democratic Socialists of America members marched in Washington, D.C., carrying signs that said, "SOCIALISM BEATS FASCISM," equating the incoming Trump administration to "fascism." A new report says that language parrots the rhetoric of foreign adversaries. (Asra Q. Nomani/Fox News Digital)
"Indoctrinate them young before they can become free thinkers," said one user.

In March, the chapter held their first "Comrades With Kids hangout" in which parents were invited to bring their kids to participate in card games, crafts, and other activities, Fox News Digital found, according to a prior social media post.

"Do you see what’s happening?? Mamdani is offering ‘free’ babysitting so they could turn your kids into socialists. They’re doing this all over the country," wrote popular conservative accounts Libs of TikTok.
Separately, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, a democratic socialist, has made child care a central part of his agenda, including through the city's new "Parents’ Night Out" program.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Members of the Democratic Socialists of America gather outside a Trump-owned building on May Day, May 1, 2019, in New York City. (Getty Images)
Mamdani's new pilot program titled, "Parents' Night Out," offers free-of-charge babysitting to parents for one night.

Nearly 300 children attended the Aug. 16 program at NYC Parks recreation centers across all five boroughs from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. Through a separate partnership with the Department of Cultural Affairs, parents were offered free and low-cost cultural experiences while their children participated in the program.
Fox News Digital reached out Mamdani’s office and DSA Charleston.
Ashley J. DiMella reports on politics for Fox News Digital.

title: Jeffries' reported meeting with Kushner about possible Trump cooperation draws left-wing backlash
summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, a New York Democrat, met with President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, reports indicate.
story: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries faces intense backlash from far-left progressives on social media after holding a closed-door meeting with President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner. The two reportedly met to discuss how Democrats and the administration could work together, leading to accusations of betrayal.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner met in recent weeks and spoke about possible issues of common ground, according to reports, landing the top House Democrat in hot water with some on the political left who have taken issue with the reported get-together.

The men talked about housing, immigration and high living costs as possible categories of common ground, the New York Times reported. Kushner, the husband of Trump's daughter Ivanka, suggested that the lawmaker should meet with White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, two individuals with knowledge of the meet-up noted, according to the outlet.
Fox News Digital reached out to Jeffries' offices and the White House on Monday.
KUSHNER GIVES HAMAS STARK ULTIMATUM: DISARM OR ISRAEL GETS US BACKING TO 'FINISH THE JOB'
Founder and CEO of Affinity Partners Jared Kushner attends the Allen & Company Sun Valley Conference at the Sun Valley Lodge on July 9, 2026, in Sun Valley, Idaho. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

"Throughout this Congress, Republicans have adopted a my-way-or-the-highway approach to governing that has failed the American people. To stop the madness, we have repeatedly made clear that an extremist approach will not work and will be met with forceful opposition," Jeffries said in a statement obtained by Fox News Digital.

"The American people want bold change and that’s what House Democrats will deliver. In every conversation that we have with the Trump administration, we will continue to make it explicitly clear that the affordability crisis is not a hoax and nothing short of transformational policy change is acceptable. We are fighting for an affordable America. The question is whether Republicans will join us," he said in the statement.
Some on the left have objected to the reported meeting between the congressman and Kushner.
SOCIALISM SURGES AMONG DEMOCRATS AS PARTY LEADERS REJECT DSA AGENDA: 'PACK OF FOOLS'

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., arrives onstage during "The New Power Structure: Black Politics in the Age of Resistance" panel during the National Association Of Black Journalists Convention on Aug. 13, 2026, in Atlanta, Ga. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images)

Zeteo founder, CEO and editor-in-chief Mehdi Hasan declared in a post on X, "The only meeting Hakeem Jeffries should be having with Jared Kushner is to tell him he’ll be subpoenaed by the House for a corruption investigation on day one of Democratic control of the House. This is just pathetic stuff from the House Dem leader."

Michelle Kinney, co-founder of The Mayday Network, wrote on X, "They should be f[---]ing hauling Jared Kushner in front of a committee, not MEETING with him. What in the absolute f--- WE ARE ALL SO SICK OF THIS S--- — ENOUGH!!!!"

Dean Obeidallah wrote on "The Dean's Report": "How could Jeffries not know the meeting would get leaked and it was the wrong thing to do?! This meeting doesn’t help Democrats win in November. In fact, now that we know about it, the result has been many Democrats slamming Jeffries online while some still defend him—causing a distraction to our real goal."
MIKE JOHNSON TAUNTS HAKEEM JEFFRIES FOR LOSING DEMS' CIVIL WAR 'IN HIS OWN BACKYARD'
The U.S. Capitol on Aug. 7, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
While Republicans currently hold a slight majority in the House of Representatives, Democrats have the opportunity to win the majority in the upcoming midterm elections.
If Democrats manage to flip control of the House, Jeffries would be a prime candidate for speaker.
Alex Nitzberg is a writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Mamdani jumps into Democratic Party feud, alleging boss seeking to subvert 'will of voters'
summary: Zohran Mamdani opposes Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn's push to add voting members to the Brooklyn Democratic Party executive committee before a fall vote.
story: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Monday rebuked a Brooklyn Democratic Party leader's proposed rule changes that critics have labeled a power grab. (WNYW)

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is opposing a last-minute push to overhaul Brooklyn Democratic Party rules, arguing the proposed changes would undermine voters after reformers made gains in the June primary.
"I very much oppose these proposed changes, by the current Brooklyn Democratic Party chair," Mamdani said. "I oppose them because they are an attempt to circumnavigate the will of voters."

The proposals from Brooklyn Democratic Party chair Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn would add more than two dozen voting members to the party’s executive committee, which will choose the party chair this fall, after a slate of reformers won 22 district leader seats in the June primary, according to the City Reporter.
NYC TAXPAYERS COULD PAY TWICE UNDER MAMDANI'S CITY-OWNED GROCERY STORE PLAN
Assemblymember Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn attends the NYC West Indian Day Parade on Sept. 1, 2025, in New York City. (Rob Kim/Getty Images)

The newly elected district leaders will not take their seats until the fall, and Bichotte Hermelyn and her supporters still hold a majority as current district leaders prepare to vote on the proposed changes Tuesday night, according to the outlet.
Bichotte Hermelyn has described the changes as an effort to broaden participation in the party.

"We want to create a perception of inclusiveness," she told NY1. In a video released by the Brooklyn Democratic organization, she said the proposals would "expand leadership" and "expand representation."
Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during an announcement on the Standing Up to ICE outreach program at the governor's office in New York City, Aug. 12, 2026. (Reuters/David Dee Delgado)

The reformers have backed longtime Sunset Park district leader Julio Peña to become the next party chair. If the proposed changes pass, the additional voting members would take part in the fall leadership election.
VICE PRESIDENT JD VANCE BLASTS MAMDANI, EL-SAYED, AOC AND OSSOFF IN RAPID-FIRE TIKTOK ROAST
Mamdani said the Brooklyn Democratic Party should reflect what New Yorkers want, rather than the kind of politics that has left people "disengaged and disaffected with politics at large."
New York Attorney General Letitia James and Public Advocate Jumaane Williams have also urged the party not to move forward with the changes.
New York Attorney General Letitia James speaks during an announcement on the Standing Up to ICE outreach program at the governor's office in New York City, Aug. 12, 2026. (Reuters/David Dee Delgado)

"New Yorkers deserve leaders who are committed to serving their communities, not rewriting rules to hold onto power," they said in a joint statement obtained by City and State New York. "Changing the makeup of an executive committee on the eve of a leadership vote goes against what we believe in as Democrats and should not move forward."
Another proposal would give former party chairs a vote in future leadership elections even after they are no longer district leaders.

According to the City Reporter, that appears to mean former party chair Clarence Norman could vote on future party leadership. Norman resigned in 2005 after multiple corruption convictions, including one for soliciting bribes from judicial nominees.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

After the leadership election, another proposed change would allow additional voting members to be appointed from each Assembly district, potentially bringing the executive committee to about 90 members.

title: Reporter's Notebook: College sports bill enters legislative 'red zone' as season kicks off
summary: As North Carolina and Texas Christian open the season in Dublin, the Senate's bipartisan college sports bill stalls amid disputes over NIL rules.
story: Fox News chief congressional correspondent Chad Pergram shares where things stand on the future of college sports on ‘Special Report.’
The college football season kicks off this Saturday with North Carolina playing Texas Christian University in Dublin, Ireland.
This marks the start of a sprint until early April when college football and basketball practically compete on a near-daily basis with MLB, the NFL, the NBA and NHL.

This college football season begins with lawmakers falling short of a goal to pass a bill to alter the flow of money in college sports. And despite recent momentum, lawmakers may be lucky to pass the bill when the clock shows zeroes on April 5 in Detroit and the NCAA crowns its next basketball Final Four champion.
PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT STALLS IN OVERNIGHT SENATE SHOWDOWN, VOTE PUSHED TO SEPTEMBER AFTER CHAOTIC EVENING
The NCAA crowns its next basketball Final Four champion on April 5 in Detroit. (Getty Images)

President Trump demanded that the Senate stay in session this month to pass a bipartisan college sports measure. That wasn’t going to happen simply because the bill’s not ready yet. The measure didn’t even secure a specific agreement for a test vote when the Senate returns in September. Senate Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, said there was a deal for a vote at some point. However, an unrelated bill to regulate cryptocurrency marshaled a concrete time for a test vote on the afternoon of Tuesday, Sept. 15. The college sports measure didn’t head into the August recess with that level of certainty.
But the one thing that is certain? Intercollegiate athletics face myriad problems.
"College sports right now is in crisis. It is chaos that is ripping college sports apart," said Cruz.

"I think that the arms race that exists now where people are just paying any amount of money from a system is not the right way to get this done," said Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash. She’s the top Democrat on the Senate Commerce Committee and helped craft the bipartisan legislation with Cruz.
CLOCK IS TICKING AS SENATORS TED CRUZ, MARIA CANTWELL PUSH FOR SEC, BIG TEN BUY-IN ON COLLEGE SPORTS BILL

Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, talks to Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., before a Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee confirmation hearing in Washington, D.C., on Jan. 15, 2025. (Samuel Corum/Getty Images)

The measure establishes a national standard for athlete compensation — including NIL — for the use of name, image and likeness of athletes. It also limits them to one transfer without losing eligibility within a five-year window.
But understanding the bill’s remedies is challenging.
"[The bill] seemed pretty dense when I read it," yours truly observed to Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., one afternoon in a hallway of the Dirksen Senate Office Building.
"It's dense as hell," replied Kennedy. "And that’s a legal term."

The measure raises the ceiling of money schools can use to compensate athletes. It essentially allows "third-party entities," like athletic footwear or equipment manufacturers like Under Armour or Nike, to pipeline additional money to schools.

Naturally, football and men’s basketball score most of the money under the current system. But lawmakers worry that women’s athletics and smaller sports like volleyball, lacrosse and soccer could evaporate unless Congress intervenes.
"It's the revenue from football and maybe basketball, but mostly football that funds everything else," said Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del.

The college sports bill seemed to gain traction in late July when the Big Ten and SEC — the most muscular of all college athletic conferences — announced their support of the legislation. Lawmakers could try to write a bill all they wanted, but with all due respect to the Mid-American Conference and Mountain West, the measure wouldn’t go anywhere unless the Big Ten and SEC were on board.

It was thought that the college sports package might get a test vote before the August recess, but a band of conservatives claimed the legislation fell short when it came to protecting women from competing against men.
"It looks like a bunch of trial lawyers drew this thing up," said Sen. Tommy Tuberville, R-Ala., a former Division I football coach who ran programs at Ole Miss, Auburn, Texas Tech and Cincinnati.
UNIVERSITIES ARE DESPERATE TO WIN NOW, BUT ATHLETES AND THE NATION BOTH LOSE
Sen. Tommy Tuberville, R-Ala., was a Division I football coach. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc. via Getty Images)

Tuberville teamed up with Sens. Jim Banks, R-Ind., and Josh Hawley, R-Mo., to craft an amendment going further in the legislation. Banks believed that the bill could undercut Indiana state law, which extends prohibitions on biological males competing in K-12 sports to college athletics. Banks expressed concern that the Cruz/Cantwell bill "would preempt Indiana’s law." The Indiana Republican asserted that he couldn’t support the legislation as written.
However, President Donald Trump torched those who said the bill failed to bar men from playing women’s sports at any level.

"Nobody has done more to protect Women Athletes than me — and this Bill CLEARLY protects the Laws in 27 States protecting Women's Sports, and banning Men from Women's Sports. Anyone who tells you differently is LYING!" thundered the president on Truth Social.

Trump worried that without adoption of this legislation, "Programs will be canceled, Women's and Olympic Sports will go away, the fans will be robbed, and Universities will go broke." He then asked the Senate to "stay in D.C. until it passes."
Despite the president’s advocacy, that wasn’t going to happen. However, the legislation does have a new set of downs — thanks to the Big Ten and SEC.
The Congressional Black Caucus (CBC) opposes the bill. In a statement, the CBC said the package fails to incorporate "perspectives of Black athletes."
Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., is the only former Division I football player in the Senate, competing as a tight end for Stanford. He opposes the bill.
"There are a lot of people who have substantive objections with that bill that should give us all pause," said Booker.
THE "PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT" HAS A FATAL FLAW: IT DOESN’T PROTECT WOMEN | RILEY GAINES

Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., speaks alongside Democratic Senate Judiciary Committee members during a news conference on the nomination of acting Attorney General Todd Blanche on Capitol Hill on July 15, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Eric Lee/Getty Images)

So the Senate essentially took a timeout on the bill with the August recess. As any fan knows, timeouts are essential in sports. They allow teams to regroup. Rehydrate with water or Gatorade. Players to catch their breath. Coaches to draw up a special play to bring the team to victory.

It’s not known what the play call might be from Cruz, Cantwell or even Trump. Or if anything would work. Some skeptics believe the Senate’s decision to leave Washington without the locked-in test vote could cost the bill momentum — compared to the deal dictating the test vote on the cryptocurrency legislation.
The University of Oklahoma led the nation in red-zone efficiency last season. The Sooners scored touchdowns more than 97% of the time when moving the ball within 20 yards of the end zone.
Ninety-seven percent is a ridiculously efficient figure. The Philadelphia Eagles were the NFL’s best red zone team last season, scoring touchdowns around 70% of the time.

The U.S. Senate is not the gridiron. But it’s clear that the bill to regulate college sports has now entered the legislative red zone. A lot of legislation gets this close to the goal line, but senators rarely enjoy the success of the Sooners or Eagles when it comes to punching it in.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
That’s why it’s possible that this legislative drive could stall — despite a steady march down the field.
Chad Pergram currently serves as Chief Congressional Correspondent for FOX News Channel (FNC). He joined the network in September 2007 and is based out of Washington, D.C.

title: Vulnerable GOP senator breaks with Trump on 2 key issues as Vance makes stop without her
summary: Susan Collins skips JD Vance's Maine visit while opposing Trump's 50% tariffs on Canada and new postal service rules restricting mail-in voting.
story: Vice President JD Vance will not be joined by Republican Sen. Susan Collins on Monday during his stop in Maine, a top 2026 midterm battleground state. (Credit: C-SPAN - Aug. 22)
Sen. Susan Collins of Maine, a moderate Republican seeking re-election in a blue-leaning state, is not joining Vice President JD Vance on Monday as he stops in her home state of Maine.

Collins, who at times has opposed President Donald Trump's legislative priorities, is a top target for Democrats this year as she runs in a midterm race that's among roughly a dozen that will determine if the GOP holds onto its slim Senate majority.

Vance's stop in Maine comes as Collins opposes Trump's move this past weekend to impose 50% tariffs on a range of goods from Canada, which shares a long border with Maine. And the senator is also opposed to new U.S. Postal Service rules that, if implemented, could rein in mail-in voting.

The vice president on Monday delivered remarks in Brewer, Maine, at Compotech, a defense technology manufacturer. It's the second stop this year by Vance in Maine and the second time that Collins has not teamed up with the vice president.
SUSAN COLLINS DROPS BRUTAL REMINDER OF DEMOCRAT CHALLENGER ROCKED BY ACCUSATIONS

Republican Sen. Susan Collins, left, said scheduling conflicts prevented her from joining Vice President JD Vance in Brewer, Maine. (Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images; Brendan SMIALOWSKI / AFP via Getty Images)
"I am already scheduled on Monday, so I will not be able to join the vice president," Collins told reporters on Saturday.

The Senate was in session when Vance held an event in Bangor, Maine, in May, and Collins stayed in Washington. The senator holds a historic attendance record of casting over 10,000 consecutive roll call votes in the Senate dating back three decades.

But Collins, speaking to reporters as she marched in the annual Madison-Anson Days parade, her seventh parade this summer, highlighted that she teamed up last week with Energy Secretary Chris Wright when he stopped in Maine to tour a federally funded battery storage project in Lincoln built on the site of a closed paper mill.
"I really appreciated Secretary Wright's presence," Collins said.
WHAT THE LATEST FOX NEWS POLL IN MAINE'S CRUCIAL SENATE RACE SHOWS

Collins, who was one of a small group of Republicans who voted to convict Trump in a 2021 Senate trial after the House impeached him following the Jan. 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol, has at times voted against the Trump administration's wishes.
"I still think imposing new tariffs on Canada is a mistake," Collins said on Saturday.

Collins also referred to the proposed U.S. Post Office rule to implement a Trump executive order to rein in mail-in voting by refusing to deliver absentee ballots in states that have not turned over their raw voter rolls to the Justice Department or Department of Homeland Security.
"Mail-in ballots are very important to the people of Maine," Collins said. "I do not support restrictions that make it more difficult for seniors to cast votes on Election Day via the mail."
WHO'S UP AND WHO'S DOWN: CHECK OUT THE FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS ON THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS
Republican Sen. Susan Collins speaks with a Maine voter as the longtime GOP senator kicks off a statewide bus tour, on Friday, August 14, in Kittery, Maine. (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News)

Collins says she supports the House version of the federal SAVE America Act (Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act), which mandates documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote and a photo ID for federal elections. But she joined three other Republicans and all Democrats to vote against advancing a Senate version of the bill, which is a top Trump priority.

Collins has also taken issue with the Trump administration over its crackdown on illegal immigration, and its aggressive deportation efforts. The administration received backlash following the fatal shootings by federal enforcement agents of two U.S. citizens in Minnesota who were protesting immigration operations. And the issue flared again this summer, after a fatal ICE shooting in Biddeford, Maine.
Democrats, including her Senate challenger, former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson, have repeatedly linked her to Trump, and heavily criticized her for her past funding for ICE.
DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Troy Jackson speaks as he became the Maine Democratic Party's choice to be their U.S. Senate nominee to replace Graham Platner on the ballot in November on July 25, 2026, in Bangor, Maine. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Collins is the only Republican senator running for re-election in a state then-Vice President Kamala Harris carried in the 2024 election. And highlighting her differences with the president and his administration may be beneficial to Collins as she woos independent voters and even some Democrats.
Vance, during his May stop in Maine, said, "Sometimes I get frustrated with Susan Collins."

"I almost wish that she was more partisan. But the thing I love about Susan is she is independent, because Maine is an independent state. And, frankly, if she was as partisan as I sometimes wish that she was, she would not be a good fit for the people of Maine," Vance continued.
Vance added, "Let’s give a shoutout to Susan Collins, who’s doing a great job."
Jackson's campaign, in a social media post ahead of Vance's visit, called the vice president "Susan's pal."
The vice president reiterated those sentiments in his Monday address in Brewer, Maine, calling Collins his "dear friend."
Vice President JD Vance speaks at Compotech headquarters in Brewer, Maine, U.S., August 24, 2026. (Anna Moneymaker/Reuters)

"As you know, Susan is the most independent member of the United States Senate and, as the president of the United States Senate, she sometimes makes my job a little bit harder. But she makes it harder because she’s coming to work every single day and fighting not for a political party… she comes to work every single day and fights for the great people of Maine and I’ve seen it," Vance said.
Jackson, in a social media post and video ahead of Vance's visit, took aim at Vance and Collins.
"I'm sure JD Vance loves her because she's doing everything that he wants for her, but she's not doing it for Maine people," Jackson argued in an accompanying video.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Vance was joined in Brewer by former two-term Republican Gov. Paul LePage, who is the GOP nominee in Maine's 2nd Congressional District.
The most rural district, the largest in the eastern U.S., is a top flip opportunity for the GOP, with moderate Democratic Rep. Jared Golden declining to seek re-election this year.
Paul Steinhauser covers the national campaign trail from coast to coast for Fox News

title: Alaska Senate race’s absurd name problem gets even harder to untangle
summary: Former Anchorage Mayor Dan A. Sullivan endorses incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan over a third Dan Sullivan accused of being a Democratic plant.
story: Fox News correspondent Matt Finn reports on the competitive Senate primaries in Alaska on 'Special Report.'

Former Anchorage Mayor Dan Sullivan is taking sides in Alaska’s unusual same-name Senate fight, endorsing incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan over a third Dan Sullivan, whose candidacy has already triggered legal challenges and allegations of an effort to confuse voters.

The intervention from Dan A. Sullivan adds another twist to a potentially competitive race in which Sen. Dan S. Sullivan and his Republican allies have accused teacher Dan J. Sullivan of running as a GOP candidate to siphon votes from the incumbent. Dan J. Sullivan has denied those accusations and says he is a legitimate moderate Republican challenger.
"As the OG Dan Sullivan, I urge Alaskans to vote for Sen. Dan S. Sullivan. He’s been great for Alaska," the former mayor wrote on social media.
DAN SULLIVAN ACCUSES SAME-NAME CHALLENGER OF TRYING TO 'RIG' ALASKA SENATE RACE
Former Anchorage Mayor Dan Sullivan, teacher Dan Sullivan and Sen. Dan Sullivan. (REUTERS/Mark Meyer | AP Photo/Becky Bohrer | Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

Republicans have attempted to use legal mechanisms to remove Dan J. Sullivan, who is himself running as a Republican, from the ballot. They point to the fact that he has worked with a Democratic-aligned consultant as evidence that he is part of a liberal plot to mislead voters.
Dan J. Sullivan has defended himself from the accusations by arguing that he is genuinely a moderate Republican that has real dissatisfactions with Dan S. Sullivan’s representation of the state.
It is unclear how many Dan Sullivans live in Alaska.
Alaska has a unique electoral system, something Republicans have argued could further contribute to confusion when voters head to the polls in November.
GOP SENATOR, EX-HOUSE DEM EMERGE FROM ALASKA’S ‘JUNGLE PRIMARY’ DESPITE FAR-LEFT MEDDLING
Dan J. Sullivan, who has filed to run for U.S. Senate in Alaska, poses for a photo in Petersburg, Alaska, on June 26, 2026. (Katie Holmlund/Associated Press)

The state holds a nonpartisan primary where the top four vote-getters advance to the general election regardless of their party affiliation. Once the four candidates are chosen and Election Day arrives, Alaskans use ranked-choice voting.
Under the system, voters rank candidates in order of preference. When their first choice is eliminated, their support passes to their next choice and so on until one candidate is victorious.

Advocates of the system argue that it gives voters greater control over who ultimately wins office as well as more options to choose from. Critics, meanwhile, argue the system could cause confusion in November.

Dan S. Sullivan and Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola have advanced to the general election, though it is unclear whether Dan J. Sullivan will join them as votes are still being counted, according to the Associated Press.

Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-AK) speaks during a hearing with the Senate Armed Services Committee in the Dirksen Senate Office Building on April 30, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

Following a Republican legal challenge, the Alaska Supreme Court held last month that Dan J. Sullivan could remain on the ballot after he was initially removed by the state’s Division of Elections. Now, federal and state prosecutors are reportedly investigating whether he is part of a conspiracy to confuse voters.

title: Fla Dem Sen-nominee Angie Nixon backed abolishing Electoral College, ranked-choice voting in resurfaced clips

story: Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla., joins ‘Saturday in America’ to react to Democratic socialist Angie Nixon’s Florida primary victory, warning about what she calls Nixon’s radical agenda and highlighting Republican support in the state.

Resurfaced clips show Florida Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon supporting abolishing the Electoral College, embracing ranked-choice voting and allowing voters to register on Election Day in a series of comments Republicans are seizing on as the democratic socialist begins her general-election campaign.

5 TAKEAWAYS FROM FLORIDA SENATE PRIMARY: GOP SEN ASHLEY MOODY WILL FACE DSA'S NIXON

Republicans are seizing on Florida Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon's past remarks, including controversial election integrity reforms and explosive rhetoric aimed at Florida Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis, the Florida courts and conservatives. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

title: Birth tourism scams draw sweeping crackdown as visa revocations climb
summary: The State Department's new Birth Tourism and Prevention Task Force has already revoked more than 750 visas as officials track travel patterns worldwide.
story: State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott told Fox News Digital that the Trump administration is ramping up efforts to curb birth tourism.
The State Department is cracking down on a popular form of visa fraud through a sophisticated worldwide operation that has already revoked hundreds of visas.

The department's spokesman, Tommy Pigott, told Fox News Digital that under the direction of President Donald Trump, the American government is partnering with agencies across the globe to halt the practice of birth tourism.

Birth tourism refers to travel to the United States for the primary purpose of giving birth so a child can obtain U.S. citizenship. The practice has been linked to visa-fraud schemes in which applicants conceal or misrepresent the purpose of their travel, often while seeking entry on visitor visas. A U.S.-citizen child may also create future immigration options for family members, including the ability to petition for a parent after turning 21.
TRUMP SIGNS EXECUTIVE ORDERS TARGETING BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP, BIRTH TOURISM AFTER SUPREME COURT SETBACK
Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaks during a Cabinet meeting at Camp David on July 31, 2026, in Maryland. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

It has also become a for-profit industry, where facilitators of the fraud market their services for helping women break America's laws through "birth in the U.S." services, including arranging visa scams to get women into the country.

"The first step in that is identifying them," Pigott said. "We have consular officers around the world that work with international partners, that work for law enforcement officials to identify patterns that indicate a birth tourism network, and then when that is identified, we take actions such as revoking their visas, which was the recent announcement that we made, to make sure that we're dismantling those networks."
ABBOTT ORDERS PROBE AFTER TEXAS HOSPITAL ADVERTISES 'BIRTH PACKAGES' IN MEXICO: 'CITIZENSHIP IS NOT FOR SALE'
Earlier this month, the State Department announced that it was launching a Birth Tourism and Prevention Task Force.

"We're making adjustments because it's very unfair," Trump said. "They're building businesses around birthright citizenship. That's not the way it was supposed to work. It's a disgrace. They're buying their way in, and we're not going to let it happen."
Through the task force, government officials are now analyzing in real time travel trends by visa holders around the world that are indicative of the practice.
TEXAS GOV ABBOTT SIGNS EXECUTIVE ORDER CRACKING DOWN ON 'BIRTH TOURISM,’ SAYS US CITIZENSHIP NOT FOR SALE

In one recent case, a woman who came to the United States on a tourist visa under the impetus of a weeks-long vacation, continuously received visits from her partner, who lived outside the country. That pattern raised officials' suspicions, who understood the partner's movements as visits to the United States to support the woman in the latter stages of her pregnancy and possibly present in the country during the child's birth.

"That was an indication that this was actually a birth tourism effort here, and we were able to take action to revoke those visas," said Pigott. "So we're able to analyze those travel patterns, analyze those instances that indicate fraud, look into those, and the task force we have allows us to take that action.
More than 100 mothers traveled to the U.S. to give birth so their children could obtain citizenship and benefits, authorities said. (iStock)
Pigott provided some examples of the blatant fraud.
BIRTH TOURISM COULD SOON CARRY A SEVERE NEW CONSEQUENCE FEW WOULD RISK: 'EXISTENTIAL CRISIS'

"There were some advertisements that were being published talking about a world without borders or automatic guaranteed citizenship in their advertisements while they were pretending to offer health care services," he said. "In reality, that is fraud, and the fraud actually doesn't just end when it has to do with the birth tourism example of lying to the consular officer."

"These networks are set up in the United States and then further coach these individuals on how to not pay their medical bills," he continued. "So you have fraud when you enter the United States and then the American taxpayer is left footing the bill. It comes down to the fundamental principle: we're gonna protect the sacred privilege of American citizenship and not allow this fraud to happen."

President Donald Trump gives a thumbs up before boarding Air Force One en route back to Washington, D.C., at Cleveland Hopkins International Airport in Ohio on Aug. 11, 2026. (Jim Watson/AFP via Getty Images)
TRUMP DOJ UNLEASHES LARGEST DENATURALIZATION EFFORT IN DEPARTMENT HISTORY — AND SAYS IT’S ‘ONLY THE BEGINNING’

The task force, officially launched on Aug. 12, has already revoked more than 750 visas tied to suspected birth-tourism activity. The State Department expects that number to increase dramatically in a very short period of time.

Pigott added that under the Trump administration, visa security is an important part of a much broader overall effort to secure the border, adding that the Biden administration, "did everything they could to allow for the abuse of our legal immigration system and allowed for the unprecedented border crisis that we saw."

title: Dem House candidate's 2013 arrest resurfaces in pivotal race for control of Congress
summary: Michigan House of Representatives candidate William Lawrence was arrested in 2013 for resisting police during an Enbridge Line 5 pipeline protest.
story: Former White House Deputy Chief of Staff Karl Rove and pollster Mark Penn analyze Michigan primary voting data showing candidate Abdul El-Sayed winning college towns, including Ypsilanti, by 53 points, while candidate Haley Stevens won Flint and Wayne County precincts.
A far-left candidate running for the House of Representatives in Michigan was arrested for resisting police during a 2013 protest.

William Lawrence, co-founder of the progressive Sunrise Movement, is challenging Rep. Tom Barrett, R-Mich., in one of the most closely-watched elections in the country. With so few congressional seats still expected to be up in the air, a victory there could be decisive for whichever party wins control in November.

Fox News Digital obtained documents that show Lawrence was among a group of people arrested in 2013 during a demonstration against the Enbridge Line 5 pipeline, a 645-mile piece of infrastructure running crude oil and natural gas between Wisconsin and Ontario — with Michigan in between.
SUNRISE MOVEMENT CO-FOUNDER DEFEATS ESTABLISHMENT-BACKED DEMS IN PIVOTAL MICHIGAN RACE

House candidate William Lawrence speaks at a rally with Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez in Lansing, Mich., on July 19, 2026. (Andrew Roth/Sipa USA via Reuters)

He and others chained themselves to machinery in protest of the pipeline, which helps the U.S. meet critical energy needs but has also been a subject of pushback by environmental groups and indigenous tribes whose land the pipeline partially runs through.

The defendants were charged with trespassing, as well as resisting and obstructing a police officer. The documents stated that Lawrence and three others had to be cut off of the equipment but were then arrested without incident.
DSA CANDIDATE PUSHES FEDERAL AI DATA CENTER MORATORIUM WITH MICHIGAN EARLY VOTING UNDERWAY
Lawrence himself previously posted on X, "Defund the Police!" in May 2020. A tweet the following month called to defund the Lansing, Michigan, police, specifically.

He told Fox News Digital in a statement this weekend, "I don't support defunding the police. I follow the lead of first responders and gun violence prevention advocates I have met with here in the district, who support increased funding for youth programs, mental health resources, and community violence intervention, working in collaboration with law enforcement."
His campaign also pointed out the conviction was expunged under Michigan state law.

He's also since addressed the arrest himself on Instagram. He said in a video earlier this year that he "took a stand" against energy company Enbridge, adding, "Was it righteous? Absolutely. Was it wise? Perhaps not."

Michigan congressional candidate William Lawrence shared this image on Instagram when he opened up about his 2013 arrest during an environmental protest. He and others chained themselves to machinery in defiance of an oil and gas pipeline. (Instagram/@wewill2026mi)

"The fact is, they were back operating that afternoon, while my collaborators and I faced legal consequences for years," he said. "I wouldn't advise you do what I did, but my conviction remains, and you can always count on me to fight for pure Michigan and our water."
DEMOCRATIC GROUP LAUNCHES $15M WAR ON DSA AFTER SOCIALIST PRIMARY WINS: 'MORTAL DANGER'
While Lawrence was backed by progressive groups in his primary election, he has since said he's left the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) as his general race begins to heat up.
But it did not stop House Republicans' campaign arm, the National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC), from tying him to the far-left.
Rep. Tom Barrett speaks at Van Andel Arena in Grand Rapids, Michigan, on Nov. 4, 2024, before former President Donald Trump holds his final campaign rally ahead of Election Day. (Jeff Kowalsky/AFP)

"Socialist felon William Lawrence is a radical far-left liberal who puts his extreme climate agenda ahead of common sense and the priorities of hardworking Michiganders. Lawrence’s extreme agenda makes one thing clear: he is far too radical for Mid-Michigan and can’t be trusted to put Michigan families first," NRCC spokesman Zach Bannon said.

Republicans are facing an uphill battle to keep control of the House this year, with the party in power traditionally facing significant losses during the midterms. But the far-left insurgency that's gripped the Democratic Party has given the right new hope that they could buck historic political trends.

title: Card skimming scam is stealing food benefits nationwide
summary: A single card skimmer can generate $1 million in stolen funds, and Secret Service video shows criminals installing them in under two seconds.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

You swipe your card at the checkout, grab your receipt and walk away. Nothing looks unusual. However, a device sitting right on top of that payment terminal may have copied your card information and PIN.

U.S. Secret Service agents recently swept hundreds of retailers across Los Angeles looking for skimmers. What they found shows how sophisticated these devices have become and how difficult they can be to spot.

This card skimming scam is especially serious for people who rely on Electronic Benefit Transfer, or EBT, cards. Many of those cards still depend on magnetic-stripe technology that criminals know how to exploit.
INSIDE NYC'S 'PERFECT SCAM': LUXURY CARS, DUSTY SHELVES AND THE EBT SECRET BEHIND THE COUNTER
U.S. Secret Service agents found sophisticated skimmers on payment terminals during a Los Angeles sweep targeting suspected fraud. (U.S. Secret Service)
New! Free live CyberGuy class: Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats

Join us Saturday, Aug. 29, at 10 a.m. ET for a free CyberGuy LIVE class covering five simple steps to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will explain how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed. You’ll also receive our financial protection checklist, and every registrant will get a link to the class recording afterward.
Reserve your free spot today at CyberGuyLive.com.
Secret Service finds skimmers hiding in plain sight

One of the most unsettling parts of the investigation is how quickly criminals can install a skimmer. Surveillance video from the investigation captured a suspect placing one over a payment terminal in less than two seconds. From there, the fake reader sits directly over the real terminal. When someone swipes a card, the device can capture account information and the PIN used during the transaction.

We have previously shown you how skimmers and shimmers can steal your payment information. What stands out now is how convincing these newer devices can look. During the Secret Service sweep, agents found a skimmer that blended closely into the legitimate payment terminal. It even had what appeared to be a security hologram.

Agents had to pry the device off. Inside, they found miniature electronics and a wireless transmitter. That transmitter can send stolen information to a criminal nearby. The person who installed the skimmer may not have to return and remove it to collect the data.
A single skimmer could lead to huge losses
The numbers behind this crime are staggering. The Secret Service says a single skimmer can generate as much as $1 million in stolen funds.
Across the country, 32 active federal investigations span 15 states. Meanwhile, the Secret Service estimates that skimming costs consumers and financial institutions more than $1 billion each year.

The agency has also stepped up its nationwide enforcement efforts. During 2025 operations, law enforcement removed more than 400 illegal skimming devices. The Secret Service says skimming activity has increasingly targeted EBT cards.

A recent Los Angeles sweep shows how widespread the problem has become. Law enforcement visited 328 businesses and inspected 1,749 payment devices. Agents seized 16 skimmers. The Secret Service estimated those removals prevented about $16.6 million in potential fraud losses.
Why criminals are targeting EBT cards

This is where things take a troubling turn. The Secret Service says criminals intentionally target locations with heavy EBT use. That includes stores where people use government benefits to buy groceries.

Many credit and debit cards now offer chips or contactless payment. However, many EBT transactions still require a magnetic-stripe swipe. That gives criminals an opening. A skimmer can capture the information stored on the magnetic stripe. Criminals can then copy that information onto another magnetic-stripe card. If they also capture the victim's PIN, they can use the cloned card to steal benefits.

For people who rely on those benefits, the impact can be immediate. Victims may discover their accounts have been drained when they try to buy groceries or pay for everyday necessities. Recovering stolen benefits can also take time, leaving families without money they were counting on.
VENEZUELAN NATIONALS CHARGED IN $529K ATM JACKPOTTING SCHEME AT I-95 REST STOPS, FEDS SAY
Tiny electronics hidden inside a skimmer can capture card data and help criminals steal information without altering the real terminal. (U.S. Secret Service)
Why EBT card security is changing

Federal officials know the magnetic stripe is a weak point. The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food and Nutrition Service says EBT fraud involving skimming is rising. The agency is working with states on modernizing SNAP EBT systems, including introducing chip cards.

Chip technology makes card information harder to copy than data stored on a magnetic stripe. Still, that transition takes time. Until more EBT systems support newer payment technology, millions of people may continue using cards that require a swipe. That leaves benefit recipients with fewer ways to avoid the very payment method criminals are targeting.
Organized crime groups are behind some skimming operations

The Secret Service says organized criminal groups are involved in some of these skimming schemes. Investigators have linked some operations to groups that travel into the United States and move between locations installing devices.

The agency has been conducting skimming operations across the country throughout 2026. Recent sweeps have focused on payment terminals at stores and ATMs where skimming activity is suspected. That kind of coordinated activity can make the devices harder to track and allow criminals to target multiple locations in a short period of time.
How to protect yourself from card skimmers
You may never spot a well-made skimmer by sight alone. Still, you can lower your risk and catch suspicious activity faster.

If a payment terminal supports contactless payments, use them. The Secret Service recommends tap-to-pay when possible. You can also use a digital wallet on your phone if the retailer supports it. For more ways to protect your cards in stores and online, see our guide on how to protect your credit and bank cards from getting hacked.

Take a few seconds before inserting or swiping your card. Look for a reader that appears loose or crooked. Also watch for damage, unusual gaps or parts that do not seem to line up correctly. The Secret Service recommends avoiding a reader if something looks altered or damaged.
IDENTITY THEFT RARELY ANNOUNCES ITSELF: 6 SIGNS YOU MISSED
Card skimmers can steal payment information and PINs in seconds, putting EBT users and other consumers at risk of fraud. (U.S. Secret Service)

Some overlay skimmers sit directly on top of the legitimate card reader. Before swiping, gently check whether anything feels loose or moves unexpectedly. Do not try to rip apart a terminal. If something seems suspicious, stop using it and notify the store.

A skimmer may capture card information while another device records your PIN. Use your hand to shield the keypad whenever you enter a PIN. That simple habit can make captured card information less useful to a criminal.

Enable alerts through your bank or card issuer so you know when your card gets used. Pay attention to small charges too. If you see something you do not recognize, contact your financial institution using the number on your card or its official app. If money has already disappeared from an account, follow our steps on what to do if your bank account is hacked.

EBT users should review their account history for transactions they do not recognize. The Food and Nutrition Service recommends checking EBT accounts regularly. It also advises changing your PIN at least once a month, particularly before your benefits are issued. If you spot an unauthorized transaction, change your PIN immediately and contact your state EBT agency.

Government agencies should not need your PIN to verify your eligibility. Do not provide your EBT card number or PIN in response to an unexpected text, phone call or email. Federal officials warn that criminals use several methods to steal benefit information, so protecting the PIN remains important even when no physical skimmer is involved.
What to do if you think a skimmer stole your card information
Act quickly once you notice suspicious transactions.

Contact the bank or organization that issued the card.Ask them to block the compromised card and review unauthorized transactions.If an EBT card is involved, contact the agency that manages benefits in your state.Change the card's PIN immediately.Also write down where you last used the card. That information may help investigators or the retailer locate a compromised terminal.Do not assume one unauthorized charge will be the end of it. Criminals who successfully copy card information may try using it again.
Contact the bank or organization that issued the card.
Ask them to block the compromised card and review unauthorized transactions.
If an EBT card is involved, contact the agency that manages benefits in your state.
Change the card's PIN immediately.
Also write down where you last used the card. That information may help investigators or the retailer locate a compromised terminal.
Do not assume one unauthorized charge will be the end of it. Criminals who successfully copy card information may try using it again.
Kurt's key takeaways

What bothers me most about this scam is that criminals are going after people who may have the fewest options to protect themselves. If I can tap my credit card or pay with my phone, I can avoid swiping altogether. Many EBT users cannot make that same choice because their cards still rely on older magnetic-stripe technology. That needs to change. These skimmers have become convincing enough to fool almost anyone, and some can transmit stolen information without the criminal ever coming back for the device. You can check the reader and keep an eye on your account, but there is only so much you can do when the payment system itself leaves you exposed. Moving benefit cards to more secure technology should be a priority, especially when families are depending on that money for food.

title: AI chatbot privacy: What your AI may know about you

story: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg outlines his ambitious open-source artificial intelligence vision, aiming to provide a personal superintelligence assistant to every user. Tech expert Kurt Knutsson joins 'Fox & Friends' to analyze Meta's latest AI model announcement, discussing what these advanced systems mean for consumer privacy and the future of digital personal assistants.

You probably tell an artificial intelligence chatbot things you would never post publicly. Maybe you ask about a health concern. Perhaps you need help sorting through a financial decision or dealing with something happening at work. Because the conversation feels one-on-one, it can be easy to forget how personal it has become.

Now, AI companies are giving their assistants more ways to remember what you tell them. In some cases, AI can also draw from activity beyond a single conversation. That raises a bigger privacy question. What happens when an AI assistant can build a more detailed understanding of you over time?

The answer depends on the service you use and the settings you choose. Your information may help personalize future responses. In some cases, your AI activity can also influence recommendations or advertising.

WHAT YOUR INTERNET PROVIDER, WEBSITES AND ADVERTISERS SEE

AI assistants can remember conversations, connect activity across services and use that context for personalization, making privacy settings increasingly important. (Samuel Boivin/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
AI chatbot privacy goes beyond model training

For years, one of the biggest AI privacy questions has been whether companies use your conversations to train future models. That still matters. However, training is only part of the picture. AI assistants can use memory to personalize future conversations. Some can draw context from connected services. Others can use certain AI interactions to help decide what content or ads you see.

So, turning off model training does not necessarily turn off memory or every form of personalization. For example, OpenAI has separate controls for model training, memory and advertising personalization. Meta also has its own rules about how interactions with Meta AI can influence content and ads.

We have previously covered the dangers of over-sharing with AI tools. As these assistants learn more about us, being selective about what you share becomes even more important. The more information an AI service can connect about you, the more personalized it can become. That can be useful. It can also create a much more detailed digital picture of your interests, routines and concerns.
ChatGPT Computer History can learn from your Mac activity

OpenAI added Computer History to the ChatGPT desktop app for macOS on Aug. 13. The optional feature lets ChatGPT and Codex use selected activity from apps and websites as context. Instead of capturing screenshots or screen recordings, OpenAI says Computer History records interaction events. It also excludes private browsing.

However, Computer History isn’t available to every ChatGPT user. OpenAI currently offers it to Pro, Business and Enterprise users. Business and Enterprise administrators must enable access before individual members can choose to turn it on. The feature is off by default.––
You can decide which apps and websites contribute information. You can also pause collection, inspect your timeline and delete history. Computer History requires Memories to work.

There are some privacy details worth knowing. OpenAI says temporary interaction-event files remain on your Mac for up to 48 hours. The company processes those events on its servers to generate memories. It says it does not retain the temporary event files after processing, unless required by law, and does not use those files for training.

Generated memory files stay on your Mac until you delete them. OpenAI also says those files are plain-text Markdown files and Computer History does not encrypt them itself. Other programs running under your macOS user account may be able to access them. That makes the feature useful, but it also gives you another reason to exclude sensitive apps and websites.
Google Search can save media you upload

Google is also expanding what can become part of your Search Services History. If Search Services History and its Save Media setting are enabled, Google can save media from your Search interactions. That can include images, files and audio or video recordings you upload or create while using supported Search services.

Google says saved media can help personalize your experience. The company may also use it to develop and improve its AI models and other technologies. If Google selects saved media for AI training, it says it disconnects that media from your Google Account first. Google says training data may then remain for up to four years. It also says it uses filters designed to remove identifying or sensitive personal information.

However, you have controls. Turning off Save Media stops Google from saving media from future Search interactions to your Search Services History. Google says future media will then stay out of generative AI training unless you submit it as feedback.

Previously saved media does not disappear when you simply turn the setting off. You need to delete it separately if you want it removed from your account. Media already selected for AI training may remain in Google's training systems after it has been disconnected from your account. That is a good example of why changing a privacy setting and deleting previously collected data are not always the same thing.
Meta can use AI conversations to personalize ads

Meta takes a more direct approach to using some AI interactions for personalization. The company announced in 2025 that interactions with its generative AI features could become signals for the content and ads people see across Meta products. Those changes took effect on Dec. 16, 2025, in most supported regions. For example, Meta says chatting with Meta AI about hiking could signal that you are interested in hiking. As a result, you could later see related recommendations or advertisements.

Meta places limits around certain sensitive subjects. The company says it does not use information from AI conversations about health or political views to show you ads. Meta also excludes religious views and several other sensitive categories from ad personalization.

Still, regular Meta AI interactions can become another source of information used to personalize your experience. That makes it worth checking your Meta privacy and ad settings before sharing something personal.
DEM SENATOR PRESSES OPENAI, ANTHROPIC FOR ANSWERS IN AI HACKING PROBE
ChatGPT, Google, Meta and Apple offer different controls over AI memory, training, connected activity and advertising personalization. (Photo by Marcin Golba/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
Meta now has an Incognito Chat option

Meta has also taken a different approach for people who want a more private AI conversation. On May 13, 2025, Meta announced Incognito Chat for Meta AI on WhatsApp and in the Meta AI app. The feature is rolling out over several months, so it may not yet appear for everyone.

Meta says Incognito Chat processes conversations inside a secure environment that the company itself cannot access. It also says those conversations are not saved, and messages disappear by default. That gives you a very different privacy experience from a regular Meta AI conversation.
We took a closer look at the feature in our guide to Meta AI's private Incognito Chat. If you have the feature, it is worth considering whenever the subject is especially personal.
Apple processes many AI requests on your device

Apple uses a more device-centered architecture for Apple Intelligence. When you make an Apple Intelligence request, an on-device model first determines whether your device can handle the task itself. If the request needs a larger model, Apple can send relevant information to Private Cloud Compute.

Apple says Private Cloud Compute receives only the information needed to complete the request. According to Apple, the content isn’t stored or made accessible to Apple. The system processes it for the request and does not retain it afterward. However, those protections apply to Apple's own Apple Intelligence system.

Apple also lets you send certain requests to third-party services such as ChatGPT. If you use ChatGPT through Apple's integration without signing into a ChatGPT account, OpenAI says it does not receive your IP address, store your requests or use them to train its models.

The situation changes if you connect your ChatGPT account. In that case, your existing OpenAI account settings apply. Your interactions may also appear in your ChatGPT history depending on your settings. So, even inside Apple Intelligence, pay attention to which AI service is actually handling your request.
ChatGPT ads can use past chats and memory if you allow it

Advertising inside AI conversations is already here. OpenAI began testing ads in ChatGPT in the U.S. on Feb. 9. Eligible Free and Go users can see ads in regions where the program is available. Plus and Pro plans remain ad-free, along with Business, Enterprise and Education plans.

OpenAI also offers Free users an ad-free option with reduced usage limits and reduced access to some tools. The privacy controls around those ads are especially relevant here. OpenAI says ads can take the context of your current conversation into account. If you enable personalized ads, past chats and memory can also contribute to ad relevance.

However, OpenAI says advertisers do not receive your conversations, chat history or memories. The company says it does not sell your data to advertisers. Advertisers receive aggregated performance information such as views or clicks. OpenAI also says ads do not influence ChatGPT's answers and remain separate from the response.

You can turn off ad personalization under ChatGPT's Ad Controls. If you do, OpenAI says ads can still use the context of your current chat, but other chat threads and memory will not inform the ads you see. That makes advertising another privacy setting worth reviewing separately from model training.
HALLUSQUATTING AI ATTACK COULD HIJACK YOUR COMPUTER

Meta says its new Incognito Chat for Meta AI will let WhatsApp users ask sensitive questions in temporary conversations that are not saved by default. (Photo by Marcin Golba/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
AI privacy rules remain a patchwork

The U.S. still does not have one comprehensive federal privacy law governing how all companies collect and use personal data. Instead, federal sector-specific laws exist alongside a growing collection of state privacy requirements. Existing consumer protection laws still apply to AI companies.

The Federal Trade Commission has warned AI companies that privacy and confidentiality promises carry legal consequences. The agency has said deceptive or unfair data practices can violate existing consumer protection laws. The FTC has also investigated consumer-facing AI chatbots, including their advertising, safety and data-handling practices. So, company privacy policies matter. They tell you what a service says it can do with information you may consider deeply personal.
How to keep your AI chatbot conversations more private
You do not need to give up AI tools to protect your privacy. However, you should decide how much information each service really needs before you start typing.

Treat a general-purpose chatbot differently from a private notebook. Avoid entering passwords or Social Security numbers. Do not paste complete banking or investment account details either. If you upload a document, review it first. Remove information the chatbot does not need.

ChatGPT's Temporary Chat does not use existing memories or create new ones. OpenAI also says Temporary Chats do not appear in your history or train its models. OpenAI says Temporary Chats are deleted from its systems after 30 days. Meanwhile, Meta is rolling out Incognito Chat for supported Meta AI users. Meta says those conversations are not saved. Use these modes when you do not want a conversation feeding future personalization.

OpenAI now lets you review a Memory summary under Settings > Personalization > Memory. You can also ask ChatGPT what it remembers about you. OpenAI says the summary may not display every detail the system can draw from your past conversations. If you find something you do not want remembered, remove it. Keep in mind that deleting one memory may not erase every source containing that information. OpenAI says fully removing information can require deleting related chats, files or other sources as well.

On the web, go to Profile > Settings > Data Controls. Then turn off Improve the model for everyone. OpenAI says your conversations will remain in your chat history, but new conversations will not train its models. The setting applies across your account. We also have a broader walkthrough showing how to opt out of AI data collection in popular apps.

If you use Google's AI-powered Search features, review Search Services History in your Google Account. Then look for the Save Media setting. Turning Save Media off prevents future media from being saved to that history. Google says it also prevents future media from being used to train its generative AI models unless you submit feedback. Remember to review previously saved material too. Turning the switch off does not automatically delete what is already there.

AI becomes far more personal when it can reach information outside the conversation. So, periodically review connected apps and services. Remove connections you no longer need. If you use ChatGPT, memory can also include relevant information accessed through connected apps when that feature is enabled. You should also protect the account itself. Our guide on how to lock down your ChatGPT account walks through additional security controls.

Do not assume that disabling AI training also turns off advertising personalization. OpenAI separates its training, memory and ad controls. Meta also provides its own ad preference controls. Take a few minutes to review each one. The more AI services know about you, the more valuable those settings become.
Kurt's key takeaways

AI gets much more useful when it remembers who you are. I can see why people want that. Repeating your preferences every time you open a chatbot gets old fast. An assistant that remembers your work or picks up where you left off can save a lot of time. Still, I would not treat personalization as an automatic yes. We're entering a period when the information surrounding an AI conversation can become almost as valuable as the prompt itself. Your memories, connected services and activity can give these systems a much deeper picture of your life. Advertising adds another layer. OpenAI now says past chats and memories can help personalize ads when you allow it. Meta already uses certain AI interactions as signals for content and advertising. For me, the safest approach is to give an AI assistant the context it needs without handing over everything it could possibly learn. Check what it remembers. Review the services you connected. Then decide whether the convenience is worth the added exposure.

Would you be comfortable with an AI assistant knowing years of your conversations if it made the service much more useful, or is there a point where personalization becomes too personal? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com
