“That’s the hard part about the business,” she said. “As you get older, it gets harder, and then you have babies! Nobody wants to see you age or see your body change.”
At the same time, Hart has acknowledged that even with a generally positive view of her body, she still has insecurities.

“I have a really good body image. But I definitely have things I wish I could change and things I get down on myself about. For example, I hate my neck — when I notice people with beautiful jawlines, I want that. But I don’t know if anybody really notices my neck except me. I try to put that in perspective.”

title: Martha Stewart Just Made a Discovery About Her Starbucks Commercial Co-Star: ‘This Guy Is Cuter!’
summary: Martha Stewart joked about “Off Campus” star Belmont Cameli appearing in her new Starbucks commercial.
story: Martha Stewart’s commercial for Starbucks’ new pumpkin spice latte is even hotter than she thought it would be.
The domestic diva had quite the reaction to seeing the ad, which, unbeknownst to her, also featured “Off Campus” star Belmont Cameli.
“Oh, pumpkin spice latte? The drink that makes us all a little more basic?” she says in the spot before a barista hands her the latte she ordered.
“This smells like my house in the fall,” she says about the treat. “It’s perfect.”
Cameli, with drink in hand, then walks up the counter asking for a straw. Martha turns and the two size each other up.
“You would get it hot,” he tells her with a wry smile.
“Should I know him?” Stewart then says to the camera as she walks away. Cameli looks on at her before turning to the camera and winking.
It turns out, Stewart may be oblivious to Cameli because he wasn’t actually on hand when she shot the commercial, at least according to the lifestyle maven.
“Wow! The actor I was interacting with while we shot the commercial was a different guy — a ‘stand in.’ This guy is cuter,” she wrote in the comments of the clip shared on Starbucks’ Instagram page.
Stewart’s reaction certainly resonated with fans.
“@marthastewart48 save some Belmont for us, bestie,” someone replied.
“@marthastewart48 as always has impeccable taste,” another person commented.
“oh my heart breaks for the poor stand in whenever he sees this,” joked another fan.
“Martha slaying in her own comment section,” someone else wrote.

While Cameli may be new to Stewart, the actor’s star is actively on the rise. After appearing in “Along for the Ride” and “The Alto Knights,” his breakout role came with Prime Video’s college hockey drama “Off Campus.”

Cameli stars as hockey star Garrett Graham opposite Ella Bright as aspiring singer Hannah Wells. After leading Season 1, Cameli and Bright are set to return for “Off Campus” Season 2, which is already filming.

title: Hoda Kotb’s Love Life Update Has Jenna and Sheinelle Begging for More: ‘What Is Happening?!’
summary: Hoda Kotb is dishing to Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones about a mysterious man she recently met on a plane, leading to “the weirdest connection in the world.”
story: Hoda Kotb shared a story straight out of a rom-com while stopping by TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle on Aug. 21.
Jenna, Hoda’s longtime former co-host, prompted the story by asking a blunt and cheeky question. “Well, everybody likes to talk about your love life. I’m going to ask you,” Jenna said.
“Well, here’s the thing,” Hoda replied, before getting into the story.
Before getting too excited, she also qualified that “this is not a real love connection.”
“I did meet someone on a plane when I was flying somewhere,” Hoda began, immediately hooking Jenna and Sheinelle Jones, who were eager to know more.
“Oh, this is romantic! Should we try to find him?” Sheinelle instantly asked.
Hoda continued to describe their brief encounter, which sounded like something straight out of a Nora Ephron movie.
“It was the weirdest connection in the world. We were both crying,” she added. “It was strange. You know, when you have one of those (conversations where) everything is firing on all cylinders?”
The feeling was mutual. Hoda said the nameless traveler was in disbelief at how much they hit it off.
“He kept saying, ‘Is this a dream? Is this real?’” she recalled.
The two parted ways after their flight. But like any rom-com fan knows, the story didn’t end there.
“Our company went to Cannes so we could talk about our company, and he was in the audience, randomly,’” Hoda shared, referring to her lifestyle and wellness venture, Joy 101.
The two met again there. “He goes, “‘Hi,’ and I said, ‘Hi,’” she said.
Then, after all that, Hoda’s story ended rather abruptly. “But then, it all kind of just went away,” Hoda said.
Jenna and Sheinelle weren’t taking that for a conclusion. “Wait,” Jenna said.
“Stop,” Sheinelle said.
“That’s the end of the story?” Jenna questioned.
Hoda admitted that wasn’t “actually the end.”
“So, we have texted recently,” Hoda shared, to Jenna and Sheinelle’s delight. Behind the camera, someone whooped.
“Look. There are connections,” Hoda said, trailing off. “I don’t know what it is.”
While they had her, Jenna and Sheinelle peppered her with questions.
Sheinelle asked whether the man was good-looking. Hoda confirmed he is “really cute” and “very handsome.”
Jenna asked if he’s single. “Yes,” Hoda said, bursting out into laughter.
“Let’s go,” Jenna said. “I don’t know what your name is, but...”
Sheinelle chimed in and said that their story gave her “’Notting Hill’ vibes.”
As for whether Hoda and the unknown flyer end up like Hugh Grant and Julia Roberts’ characters? We’ll have to wait for the next chapter.

title: Sharna Burgess Returns to ‘Dancing With the Stars’ After 5-Year Hiatus
summary: Sharna Burgess is returning to Dancing With the Stars. Here’s her history on the show.
story: The ballroom is welcoming back a familiar face for “Dancing With The Stars” Season 35.
The show’s upcoming season will feature Australian ballroom dancer and pro Sharna Burgess, as confirmed on Good Morning America’s Aug. 24 broadcast.
“I’m back in the ballroom baby,” Burgess said in the video announcement, also shared on the “Dancing With the Stars” Instagram page.
“A little birdie told us an absolute firecracker is back in the ballroom. Please give @sharnaburgess a warm welcome on her return as a #DWTS pro,” the caption read.
Burgess last took the “DWTS” stage in 2021, when she competed with her fiancé, Brian Austin Green. Green and Burgess welcomed a son in 2022 and got engaged in 2023.
The dancing pro has had a long history with the show. She first appeared as a troupe member of Season 13 in 2011, meaning that she danced in group numbers but not one-on-one with celebs.

Then, in 2013, she became a “DWTS” pro for Season 16. She came close to winning in Season 21, coming in second place with Nick Carter. She finally won the Mirrorball Trophy in Season 27, alongside Bobby Bones.
Meanwhile, she’s been a judge on the Australian edition of “Dancing With the Stars” since 2019.
Burgess is in good pro-company for “DWTS” Season 35, with a return for fellow Mirrorball winner Witney Carson already announced.

So far, four contestants have been announced for Season 35: “Love Island” and “The Traitors” alum Maura Higgins, “Summer House” star Ciara Miller, “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” sidekick Guillermo Rodriguez and Savannah Bananas star Jackson Olson.
“DWTS” Season 35 airs Sept. 15 live on ABC and simultaneously on Disney+.

title: Adam Scott Shares What Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s Wedding Was Really Like
summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding took place in front of a crowd of about 1,000 people at an iconic New York City arena, but Adam Scott says it still had the intimacy of a smaller gathering.
story: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding took place in front of a crowd of about 1,000 people at an iconic New York City arena, but Adam Scott says it still had the intimacy of a much smaller gathering.
The “Severance” star was one of the guests at the epic nuptials between the Kansas City Chiefs star tight end and the global pop superstar, set at Madison Square Garden on July 3.

“It was kind of on a grand scale,” Scott told Craig Melvin on TODAY Aug. 24. “There were more people than were at my wedding, but at its core, it just felt like a regular wedding with two people coming (together). Everyone was teared up. It was a really lovely, lovely event.”
Despite all the spectacle, the details of which have slowly trickled out from the star-studded guest list, Scott said all the emotions involved were heartfelt and genuine.
“It was incredible,” he said. “It was really terrific. The impression we had more than anything was that it was a real wedding. You had the sense that these are just people who love each other.”

Among the many people jealous of Scott for scoring a coveted invite was his teen daughter Francesca “Frankie” Scott, who is a diehard Swiftie. Craig asked the actor if going to the wedding scored him some dad points with his daughter.
“Sure did, except I didn’t bring her, so I lost some points at the same time,” Scott said. “But she stayed up and waited for us to come home that night to get all the details.”
Craig asked if Scott could reveal any of those actual details that he shared with his daughter.
“I can’t,” Scott said. “You can have her on, and she’ll tell you what happened.”
“Honestly, we would book her tomorrow if she would share,” Craig joked.

Scott attended the wedding with his wife, Naomi Scott, as well as Paul Rudd and wife Julie Rudd. The “Parks & Recreation” actor shared a photo of the two couples in their wedding guest best, with the caption, “❤️T&T❤️.”
After attending the wedding of the year this summer, Scott has now joined his castmates for the third season of “Severance,” which he said is “a few weeks in” to shooting.

He also stars in the new Netflix crime thriller “The Whisper Man,” which begins streaming on Aug. 28. Scott plays a widower whose 8-year-old son goes missing, and he reaches out for help to his estranged father, a retired cop played by Robert De Niro.

title: Jenna Bush Hager Posts New Family Photos from Summer Trip: ‘August Slipped Away’
summary: Jenna Bush Hager shared photos from her family vacation on Instagram, including one shot with her daughters, her mom, Laura, and her sister, Barbara.
story: Jenna Bush Hager is squeezing every drop of summer she can before it comes to an end.
The TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle co-host posted a carousel of pictures from her family vacation on Instagram on Aug. 23.
“I can see us lost in the memory August slipped away into a moment in time,” she captioned the photos, quoting lyrics from Taylor Swift’s song “August.”

The first image brought together multiple generations of the Bush family. It captured Jenna with her mother, former first lady Laura Bush, along with twin sister Barbara Bush and her daughter, Cora, as well as Jenna’s daughters, Mila, 13, and Poppy, 11.
Barbara and husband Craig Coyne also share son Edward, 2, while Jenna and husband Henry Hager are also parents to son Hal, 6.

Other shots showed Jenna laughing with husband Henry Hager, kids frolicking on rocks near the water, the family on the beach together, kids walking through a garden, Jenna taking a selfie with Poppy and Jenna having a laugh.
Jenna often shares photos of sweet family memories. For the Fourth of July, she posted a roundup of pics of her family soaking up time at the beach and on a boat, captioning it, “Magic of July.”
While Jenna seems to have gotten plenty of quality time with her kids this summer, she’s previously reflected on how her children will become more independent as they grow up.

“I realized that I’m not going to be in all of my kids’ memories. And that actually is a great thing,” she said in 2024 at a TODAY Mother’s Day event. “They’re starting to become really independent, and they don’t need me as much. And I’m like, ‘OK, I did something right.’”

title: Leslie Mann Shares Brutally Honest Secret To Her 30-Year Marriage With Judd Apatow
summary: Actor Leslie Mann has opened up about how she’s been able to keep her three-decades-long marriage to director Judd Apatow going strong.
story: Actor Leslie Mann has opened up about how she’s been able to keep her three-decades-long marriage to director Judd Apatow going strong.
On an Aug. 20 episode of podcast “Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce,” Mann, 54, revealed the key to the superstar pair’s marriage.
“Just accepting how hard it is and not trying to fool yourself,” Mann told host Kylie Kelce. “That’s the secret.”
She also got real about just how difficult a lasting relationship can be.

“When I see other people talking about their perfect marriages or like how they never fight or they’re I don’t know, just all the the stuff that I can’t relate to ... That’s a red flag,” Mann said on the podcast.
Mann — who’s currently promoting comedy “Spa Weekend,” which hit theaters Aug. 21 — shares two daughters, Maude Apatow and Iris Apatow, with the director. The two have been married since 1997.
She first met Judd Apatow while she was auditioning for 1996 film “The Cable Guy.” In a 2017 interview with TODAY’s Willie Geist, Mann shared that for Apatow, it was love at first sight.

“He did say to Ben, ‘There goes the future, Mrs. Apatow,’” Mann said, seemingly referencing the film’s director Ben Stiller. “But I think he may have said that about Heather Locklear and, like, J Lo too.”
While on the recent podcast, Mann told Kelce that while the couple has their tiffs, she and Apatow, 58, still have a valuable connection.
“We find each other entertaining and funny — sometimes,” Mann said. “He is my best friend and I tell him everything.”
She added, however, that Apatow may not always reciprocate.
“I don’t know if he tells me everything. It comes out at certain times, and then sometimes he, like, shuts it down,” she said, before agreeing with Kelce that “it’s a universal man thing.”
Ultimately, Mann said, the relationship is an “important” one.
“You have a witness to your life also,” Mann said of marriage. “So your kids, growing all the memories — that’s important. That’s a that’s a big one.”

Mann and Apatow have not only been romantic partners, but they’ve also shared a professional relationship as collaborators. Beyond “The Cable Guy,” The pair have worked on “Knocked Up” and “Funny People,” “This is 40” and much more.
In a 2012 interview with Elle, Apatow said that Mann was a critical reason why he began to write better roles for the women in his projects.

“Leslie would always say, ‘There aren’t good roles for women, the female parts aren’t developed, the women are serving the men,’” he told the outlet. “And just seeing the stack of scripts she had to read showed me how little effort was put into making great female characters.”

title: People Are Divided On Margaret Qualley’s ‘Barefoot Sandals’ Red Carpet Look
summary: Actor Margaret Qualley, who’s currently promoting the upcoming Ridley Scott film “The Dog Stars,” stepped onto the red carpet at the film’s world premiere Aug. 20, wearing a pair of Chanel’s “shoeless shoes.”
story: The internet isn’t toe-tally sure if these are hot or not.

Actor Margaret Qualley, who’s currently promoting the upcoming Ridley Scott film “The Dog Stars,” stepped onto the red carpet at the film’s world premiere Aug. 20, wearing a pair of Chanel’s “shoeless shoes.” The look instantly went viral for its controversial aesthetic, with some loving the high-fashion shoes and others saying that they weren’t shoes at all.

The shoes, part of Chanel’s Resort 2027 collection, consist of black heels that are strapped to the feet with two sets of laces. There isn’t much of a sole. So when wearing these shoes, the majority of the wearer’s feet are bare and touch the ground.

The internet wasn’t quite sure what to make of the moment. One social media user on X joked that the shoes were just a reflection of “shrinkflation.  And another jokingly predicted that next season, the fashion brand will likely “sell the front part.”
However, there were still a number of people who were living for it. A social media user wrote, “chic this chic that. THIS is chic, to me”
Another person also described the shoes as “kinda chic high key.”

The shoes have been drawing a lot of opinions since they debuted on the runway in April at a show in the French seaside resort city of Biarritz.  At the time, Chanel’s creative director Matthieu Blazy, had already sparked debate for the design. And fashion insiders weren’t even united in their stances.
“Is it half the price as well?” one person wrote on Instagram.
Another described the shoes as an “updated anklet for the beach!”
So where do you stand on these haute couture shoes?

title: From Música Mexicana to Country, Carin León Is Making His Own Rules
summary: Mexican singer-songwriter Carin León has forged his own path when it comes to música Mexicana. Most recently he is dipping his toes into the American country space.
story: Authenticity is among Carin León’s core values, whether it’s with his music, clothes or way he carries himself.

That’s why the 37-year-old Mexican singer-songwriter has forged his own path when it comes to música Mexicana. Known for his banda and norteño roots, León isn’t afraid to dabble in different genres, most recently dipping his toes into the American country space.

His latest album, “MUDA,” is a mix of what audiences have grown to love from León’s contemporary sound, along with salsa, pop and country music. He’s previously described the project as a “representation of my unfulfilled musical desires.”

“I love regional Mexicano, obviously, but at the same time when I was a kid I was listening to rock music to rap music, a lot of R&B, soul,” León tells TODAY.com, alternating between Spanish and English. “This combination of genres and combination of ideas, it’s very interesting for me to mix all of those things and get to this whole new style in the way of my singing, making music and dressing.”

León has dominated Latin charts for years, with a dozen No. 1s on the Regional Mexican Airplay chart along with several No. 1s on the Latin Airplay chart. He’s also won four Latin Grammys and two Grammy Awards. He’s proving that the crossover is very much alive and well as he ventured into the country and soul space with collaborations with Kane Brown, Cody Johnson and Leon Bridges.
In 2025, he worked with Kacey Musgraves on the Spanglish hit “Lost In Translation.” He also teamed up with Jelly Roll on “Lighter,” a song featured on the official FIFA World Cup 2026 album.

On working with Musgraves, León says it’s wonderful to collaborate with artists “who have inspired” me. He also teases that, specifically in the country genre, he has “a lot of surprises” with “interesting” stars coming up.

While artists like Bad Bunny, J Balvin, Karol G and others have light up the global airwaves with reggaeton hits, León is making his presence seen in places that regional Mexican artists haven’t typically touched.
He’s performed at the Nashville’s Grand Ole Opry, known as one of country music’s biggest stages, and became the first Latin artist ever to perform at both Coachella and Stagecoach in the same year.

Currently on his “De Sonora Para El Mundo” North American tour, he’s partnered with Mexican beer brand Victoria to give fans the chance to win a custom limited-edition Cobija jacket, created by Mexican American designer Brenda Equihua, as well as a trip and tickets to one of his shows.
Inspired by his last name León, which translates to lion, the brown and tan jacket has the face of a lion stitched on the back. The artist says he wants one for himself to match with the lucky fan.
Up next, León is making history as the first Latino artist to headline Sphere in Las Vegas. The artist will perform at the iconic venue for two weekends, Sept. 4-6 and Sept. 11-13.

“It’s a whole different production because (the venue is) an amazing tool for us to express a lot of things that we can’t express regularly in a show,” he says, describing the creative process and production as a “dive into my brain.”
“See the world through my eyes, that’s the whole concept of Sphere,” he says. “How I see (my home state) Sonora, how I see my music, how I see the world through the eyes of a little boy from Sonora.”

León and his team have been preparing for his Sphere shows for about a year and a half. He attended a Backstreet Boys show to see Sphere in action, saying, “I’m such a fan of music. It (blew) my mind away.”
“I started to shake because I’m gonna be there,” he says. “It’s a stage that you have to respect. I’m very excited at this moment more than nervous.”
Whether it comes to music or his Mexican vaquero (cowboy) aesthetics he says in Spanish: “Las reglas son para quebrarlas,” which translates to, “The rules are meant to be broken.”

As he continues to break the mold of what a regional Mexican artist should look like, León says the most fulfilling moment so far this year is realizing that the risks he took have been worth it and accepted by fans.
“At first with my music, with the way I dress — I was scared to do it my way because it was different,” he says. “And I thought I would be punished by my audience or my fans.”
He adds that the “most important thing is to be real and authentic and when you lose that fear (of being criticized), that is the best thing that can happen to an artist.”

title: Love Jimothy? Meet Meemers, The Adorable Cat With Short Spine Syndrome
summary: For fans of the perfectly imperfect Jimothy the Raccoon, there’s now another furry friend over which we can all obsess.
story: For fans of the perfectly imperfect Jimothy the Raccoon, there’s now another furry friend over which we can all obsess.

Readers, meet Meemers: The adorable rescue cat who has short-spine syndrome, the same condition that Jimothy is also believed to have. The two-and-a-half-year-old feline, who’s based in Bloomington, Illinois, recently went viral for her barely-there neck and resemblance to Seattle’s beloved raccoon. One video of Meemers, posted Aug. 18, has drawn more than 41 million views as of Aug. 22.

Owner Katie Dahlen, who previously worked at the shelter where Meemers was found, has always loved making clips for social media. But, Dahlen tells TODAY.com, that she never expected the video of Meemers to go viral seemingly overnight.

“I missed making videos, and I was like, ‘Well, I have this awesome cat, and I want to share her with people,’” Dahlen says. “I just didn’t realize how big she would blow up in a 24-hour span. It was crazy.”
In the video, Meemers, in her black, fluffy glory, simply sits down. There’s a few shots of Meemers giving her best Blue Steel as well. And it’s truly easy to see why she’s so beloved.
“Sensational whiskers / body tea / no notes 🖤” one fan replied.
Another demanded a collab between Meemers, Jimothy and Tilly, the famous pup who also has short spine syndrome.

Meemers is certainly unique. From her shoulders to the base of her tail, she’s only about seven-and-a-half inches long. She also has a slight tail deformity. For Dahlen, who’s had Meemers for over a year now, it was love at first sight.

“She was actually left at the shelter in a box outside,” Dahlen says of the shelter at which she was working at the time. “Literally, from the day she came in, I was like, ‘She needs to come home with me.’”
Meemers was, at first, not in the greatest shape, Dahlen says. The fur around her butt was matted and there was an abscess in the area as well, Dahlen explains.

“The owner had tried to shave her, so you could tell they cared, but maybe they didn’t have the resources, and they were embarrassed about walking her in through the doors,” Dahlen says. “So they left her out front.”
After Meemers was given a course of antibiotics and some TLC, she was ready to head home with Dahlen. And since July 2025, Dahlen said she and her husband have been enjoying their adorable cat.

Given her deformities, Meemers has had to make a couple of adjustments in order to thrive, Dahlen says. She doesn’t climb much and she’s unable to jump. Because her organs are squished in her very small body, she needs to be held a certain way, Dahlen says. The feline also overheats quite easily.

“I always equate her to being kind of like a pug, where she overheats easily if it’s too warm outside,” she says. Dahlen adds that if Meemers over-exerts herself, she’ll start panting. “So a lot of her supervised outside time in her backyard is in the evening when it’s cooler.”
Dahlen points out that Meemers has “virtually no neck,” so she’s unable to successfully groom her own back. That’s where Dahlen comes in.

“I brush her multiple times a day. If I’m sitting down, watching TV in the evening, she’s sitting on my lap and I’m grooming her,” Dahlen says. “She gets the occasional bath because I can only redistribute the oils in her coat so much with brushing.”
Though none of that has stopped Meemers from having an infectious personality. She’s a people person, er, cat, Dahlen says. And she’s quite social.
“She loves people,” Dahlen says. “I can literally take her out like anywhere on leash.”
Meemers also loves being pet, and often returns the favor with chatty little meows that Dahlen likens to the sound that Spongebob’s pet Gary the snail makes.
“She loves to be held, but you have to hold her right,” Dahlen says. “When you pet her, she will talk.”
As for Meemers’ incredible name? Well, Dahlen says it’s actually a moniker that evolved from the cat’s original name Mila.

“I was calling her ‘Mimi.’ I was calling her ‘Mealy Bug,’ and then ‘Meemers’ just kind of came up,” Dahlen says of the cat’s now one true government name. “Then she was really only responding to that.”
Dahlen says she’s been pleased with the positive reception to her Meemers and hopes that fans can learn from the sweet cat.
“Give special needs cats a chance,” Dahlen says. “They definitely do require a little adaptation at home, but they are so worth it.”

title: Man Who’s Rated Over 300 Benches Gives Out Only Perfect Score For The Sweetest Reason
summary: Sam Wilmot, who runs @ratethisbench on Instagram, finally gave out an elusive perfect score to the bench at which he got married.
story: Bench your plans, take a seat and listen to a tale that’s sweet as can be from top-to-bottom.

Sam Wilmot, a 29-year-old based in Bristol, England, has rated more than 300 benches through his Instagram page @ratethisbench, he tells TODAY.com. With a strict criteria in place, Wilmot has never given out a perfect 10 — that is, until he recently revisited one particular bench with his beau, Sophie, on their wedding day.

The post about the bench — one that sits outside of the striking 13th century church St. John the Baptist in the village of Old Sodbury — has since gone viral as shocked fans have long been waiting for that elusive 10/10. Wilmot, who’s not in it for fame, says that for him, the bench will forever be associated with the “best day of my life,” Wilmot tells TODAY.com.

“I’d always held back a mark for the “wow” factor, and previously scored this bench a 9/10. But the overwhelming feeling of joy and awe in this moment is the wow,” Wilmot wrote in the caption of the photo, posted in June. “No moment or bench will ever come close to this for me, I can proudly say I have found my 10. In Sophie, and this bench. Sophie Alicia Wilmot, I love you.”

Wilmot has rated everything from a department store bench that featured Paddington Bear, which scored a 6/10, to a carved, wooden bench outside of England’s National Coal Mining Museum, which was given a 5/10. And each post comes with a description and some interesting facts and reflections in addition to the score rationale.

To make things fair, Wilmot scores everything on a rubric, he says. There’s up to three marks for location and view, one mark for having a concrete or solid base for accessibility in all seasons, another mark for being made out of wood and a mark for having a plaque or dedication, he says.
Wilmot also considers functionality. There’s a mark for having an armrest or back support along with another one for curvature of the seat, an important aspect of comfortability, he says.
“Then, really, the tenth mark is a ‘wow factor,’” Wilmot says. “Something that makes it stand out significantly, or is inspiring.”

And Wilmot is firm on the criteria. For example, the Giant’s Chair, a striking art installation in Aberystwyth, Wales, was given a rating of 4/10. The view, according to his rationale, was lovely. But the bench didn’t perform so well in some other important ways.

“The bench itself would fit 3 people, but somewhat uncomfortably. Due to it’s size and dimensions, the back rest is near redundant based on ones inability to sit upright using it due to the depth of the seat,” Wilmot wrote. “It’s not an easy climb up either. But it is different, and offers an unspoiled view of the valley which falls away at your feet.”

The 10/10 bench, however, hit all the marks. Not only that, Wilmot says, it’s representative of the couple’s journey together, which is important given the fact that so much of the account has been made possible because of his wife’s support. In fact, since November 2019, she has been the page’s photographer.

“Ratethisbench existed prior to meeting Soph, but it would not exist without her or have become what it is today without her willingness to accept random adventures for new benches and capture the moment for me. Our first exchange 7-years ago was bench related and there was no telling at the time where it would lead,” Wilmot wrote in the June post. “People have tried to make out bench reviews and rankings to be boring and mundane, but there’s nothing boring about spending time outdoors and bonding with the person you grow to love whilst bench spotting.”
He added in the post that “there is no possible moment in life I will cherish more than sitting on my favourite bench, alongside my wife moments after marrying surrounded by our friends and family.”

The two have been to countless benches together, but the one outside of St. John the Baptist has long had meaning to the couple, he says. The pair have not only had fun chats there, but they’ve also discussed some deeper topics including big life changes and career plans, Wilmot explains. Of course, he says, the wedding topped all their other experiences at that bench.
He says that his wife actually entered his life around 5 months into his bench-rating journey. And she was immediately supportive of the idea. Perhaps it was a sign.

“She’s always been a big advocate of enjoying the journey to the benches, so she’s always been keen on the walk, the chat associated with them, and just sort of the reason and excuse to get out of the house,” Wilmot says. “So she’s really bought into that whole idea of the benches.”

With the increased interest in both the account and his story, Wilmot says he hopes that people who come across his page, walk away with an understanding that “benches themselves are a lived experience.”

“A bench isn’t necessarily a monumental thing that other people review. It’s not going to cost you the earth either,” he says. “It’s really just about the little things, enjoying the chit chat that comes with it, the sort of people you meet along the way.”

title: Anna Paquin Blasts Hollywood’s Treatment of Child Stars In Tribute To Hayden Panettiere
summary: Following the death of actor Hayden Panettiere, fellow former child star Anna Paquin spoke out about Hollywood’s treatment of its young female actors.
story: Following the death of actor Hayden Panettiere, fellow former child star Anna Paquin spoke out about Hollywood’s treatment of its young female actors.

In an Instagram post shared Aug. 21, Paquin blasted the industry, accusing it of failing to protect “pre-sexualized female, child ‘stars’” including Panettiere. Paquin, who made her acting debut in the 1993 film “The Piano,” was 9 years old when filming began. Panettiere’s television career began at 4 years old in the soap opera “One Life to Live.”

“It’s not a coincidence that so many former, specifically pre-sexualized female, child ‘stars’ have profoundly sad lives and untimely ends,” Paquin, now 44, wrote in the post, before likely referencing the deaths of Panettiere, Michelle Trachtenberg and Daveigh Chase. “We were not as protected by the ‘systems’ that look great on paper, as we are supposed to be. RIP HP, MT, DC and too many others.”

Trachtenberg died in 2025 at age 39 due to complications from diabetes. Chase died in June at age 35 from AIDS. Her father John Schwallier confirmed to NBC News that she was homeless at the time of her death.
Paquin also encouraged others who have backgrounds as child stars to reach out to her for support.

“It’s a strange small club we belong to and you are worthy of support no matter how our industry made us feel. Literally DM me,” Paquin wrote. “I believe you and I will stand by your side. You aren’t alone. Let’s have each other’s backs. It might make public disclosure less terrifying.”

Panettiere was found unresponsive Aug. 16 at a residence in Greenville, South Carolina and later pronounced dead. She was 36. Her passing has reignited discussions around the treatment of child stars. Panettiere, who’s also known for her roles in “Heroes” and “Nashville,” had begun to appear on screen when she was not yet a year old. In her book, “This Is Me: A Reckoning,” published in May, Panettiere wrote that she had “lost the chance to have a ‘normal’ childhood.”

In her memoir, Panettiere described a collection of traumatic events, including when, at 19, she was asked to get in bed with an older celebrity. The actor also described moments when a television executive kissed her on the lips, and when an Oscar-winning actor and director exposed himself to her at a party.
When she was 15 years old, Panettiere was given “happy pills” before walking a red carpet — an incident that would kickstart a long battle with drug addiction, she has said.
“I had no idea that this was not an appropriate thing, or what door that would open for me when it came to my addiction,” she said in a 2022 interview with People.

Paquin, who’s also known for her roles in “X-Men” and “True Blood” has been open about her experiences as a child star in the past. The actor, who won the Oscar for best supporting actress at age 11 for her performance in “The Piano,” told The Guardian in a 2019 interview that she’s had “some absolutely horrific experiences” as someone growing up in the industry.

“People treat people who have no power, sometimes, in ways that are completely unacceptable,” Paquin told the outlet. “But when you’re a child and you don’t know any different, and you don’t want to get into trouble, you just keep your mouth shut.”

Paquin’s latest post has drawn praise from several other former child stars including Mara Wilson, who played the titular character in 1996 film “Matilda,” and Alyssa Milano whose breakout role was as character Samantha Micelli in 1980s sitcom “Who’s The Boss?”

title: Travis Barker Shares Message His Late Mom Told Him That Fueled His Career
summary: Travis Barker says he credits his late mom, Gloria, for his successful music career.
story: Travis Barker says he credits his late mom, Gloria, for his successful music career.

The Grammy-nominated Blink-182 drummer got emotional during a recent episode of Anderson Cooper’s “All There Is” podcast while recounting his mother’s inspiring last words to him before she died of complications resulting from Sjögren’s syndrome, an autoimmune disease.
Barker, who was a teenager at the time, told Cooper he had “no clue” his mom would die.
The day before starting high school, Barker visited his mom in the hospital, where she encouraged him to follow his musical dreams.
“Luckily, I got down there the day she passed and had a chance for her to say, like, ‘Pursue music.’ Like, ‘I really want you to pursue music,’” he recalled.
The following day, a broken-hearted Barker attended his classes trying not to cry. When Cooper asked Barker if he remembered that day, the musician nodded as tears filled his eyes.
After Barker placed his head in his hand, Cooper shared a painful  memory from his own childhood.
“When my dad died, I was in fifth grade and I had a sense of shame about it for some reason,” Cooper recalled.
“Like, I remember a kid wanted to come over,” Cooper went on, his voice breaking.
After pausing, Cooper repeated, “I remember a kid wanted to come over to my house and I was angry about it because I didn’t want him to see me, like, sad. I didn’t want anyone to acknowledge it.”
“Yeah, same,” Barker said, wiping his eyes.
Though Barker was lost in anguish, he was determined to honor his mom’s last words to him.

“I had never experienced loss before that,” Barker said. “I didn’t really know a next step or step to take after that happened except to pick up where I left off and keep playing drums ... So that’s all I focused on, like head down, play the drums.”
He added, “I had this desire in me to fulfill what she said to me. I was like, I have to do it.”
Over the years, Barker has felt his mom was a kind of “angel” guiding him toward success.
“To me, she’s not just dead and gone. I do feel her presence. It’s almost ignorant to think I could just be so blessed to have everything I have now without her,” he said.

The drummer, whose life story is told in the new Hulu documentary “Travis Barker: Louder Than Fear,” endured trauma again when he was severely burned in a 2008 small plane crash that killed four people.

The crash’s only other survivor, Barker’s close friend Adam “DJ AM” Goldstein, died of an overdose the following year. After the crash, Barker struggled for years with severe post-traumatic stress disorder and a fear of flying.
Grief, for him, has been like “a wound that almost never heals” and is easily “reopened”
“I can go through days, weeks, months, not thinking about it, and then something, right, something will remind you,” Barker said.
Therapy and time spent with loved ones, including wife Kourtney Kardashian and the couple’s blended family of seven kids, whom he called his “superpower,” have helped him process the pain.

“I remember my post-traumatic doctor had said something like, ‘People go through life just expecting everything to be perfect and not everything’s gonna be perfect. Sometimes you’re gonna face adversity, right? But these things either destroy you or define you.’ And there was no way I was gonna let it destroy me.”

title: Alessandra Ambrosio’s Cushion Cut Engagement Ring Is Worth $200,000 to $400,000, Experts Say
summary: Alessandra Ambrosio’s engagement ring from her Australian jewelry designer fiancé Buck Palmer puts a modern twist on a classic “cushion cut” design.
story: Alessandra Ambrosio’s engagement ring from her Australian jewelry designer fiancé Buck Palmer puts a modern twist on a classic “cushion cut” design.
Its design is also part of a broader trend when it comes to celebrity engagement and wedding rings.

The 45-year-old supermodel announced her engagement to Palmer Aug. 11 on Instagram when she posted several images from the couple’s romantic beachside proposal. She also posted a close up of the engagement ring in another post.
In the pics, Ambrosio flaunts a whopper of a diamond ring on her left ring finger.
“It’s an elongated cushion cut,” Mallory Shelter of Shelter Jewelry tells TODAY.com of the diamond.
As for its size? “Probably six to seven carats,” Shelter estimates.
A Mix of Traditional and Trendy
The diamond is “set in a very classic bezel setting,” says Shelter.
In other words, the ring features a custom-fitted metal rim that wraps around the diamond rather than encasing it in prongs.
“It’s a sleek, modern alternative to a more traditional prong setting,” Shelter explains.
A bezel setting offers “practical advantages, especially with stones of this size.”
“They’re a more secure setting, protect the edges of the stone and are less likely to snag on clothing, which makes it a really comfortable ring to wear,” Shelter adds.

The setting’s style is trendier than ever this year, she continues, noting, “I think we’re seeing a lot of them right now because they give a vintage but modern feel. It’s a great way to have a solitaire style feel more distinctive rather than mainstream.”
The understated, “unfussy” look, Shelter adds, “feels very aligned with the current move toward quieter, more design-forward luxury.”
A Style That’s Hot With Celebrities
Anna-Mieke Anderson, founder and former CEO of MiaDonna, says the ring’s vintage look has been trendy with celebrities.
“We are certainly seeing a return to antique-inspired, metal-forward settings,” Anderson tells TODAY.com.
Zendaya’s wedding ring, for example, “is a true Georgian-inspired button-back design,” referring to a type of closed-back bezel setting that’s rooted in the Georgian era.
Taylor Swift’s ring “has a vintage-style yellow-gold bezel with hand engraving,” she adds.
“Alessandra’s (ring) belongs to that same broader movement,” explains Anderson.
Asher Wiener, CEO of Luma Jewellery, agrees Ambrosio’s ring probably features a button back — or possibly a closed back collet — setting.

“What I like is that it’s unforgiving,” says Wiener. “Close the back and light can only get in and out through the top, so the cut has to be good or the diamond goes flat on the hand. A tall claw setting will carry a mediocre stone. This one won’t.”

“The trend’s real and I think it’s a reaction to 15 years of very tall, six claw solitaires. Zendaya’s Jessica McCormack ring did most of the work, Taylor Swift’s bezel pushed it further, and we’re seeing more requests for it,” says Wiener.
A Yellow Gold Band
The band on Ambrosio’s ring is yellow gold, “almost certainly 18k,” says Wiener.

“Gold does a diamond a quiet favor nobody talks about. The warm metal reflects up into the stone and hides a warmer color grade, so an H or an I looks white in gold when it would look tinted in platinum. That’s someone buying with their eyes, not off a certificate,” Wiener explains.
What’s the Ring’s Story?
The ring “is incredibly elegant, just like Alessandra,” says Anderson.
“The elongated cushion is timeless, while the yellow-gold setting gives it warmth and modernity. This ring will never go out of style, and it will go with absolutely everything,” Anderson adds.
All three experts noted Palmer, as a designer himself, knows his way around a ring.

“He’s a jeweler, so he made it at his own bench instead of walking into a store,” says Wiener. “There’s no showing off in it. Oldest setting in the book, plain band, every decision pointing at a ring she can live in rather than one she has to look after.”
The Ring Is Likely Worth $200,000 to $400,000
The estimated cost of the ring is anywhere from $200,000 to $400,000, says Anderson, who guessed Ambrosio’s diamond was closer to seven carats than six.
“Exceptional color, clarity, provenance, or designer craftsmanship could place it above that range,” Anderson notes.
“We would need to see the grading report to confirm the diamond’s origin and characteristics,” she adds.
Wiener agrees, more or less, with Anderson’s estimate.

“If it’s natural and grades around G color, VS clarity at six carats, roughly $200,000 to $350,000 at retail. Seven carats with better clarity takes it past $450,000. The gold work is maybe $5,000 of that.
“(Palmer) is in the trade though, so what he actually paid is a fraction of the numbers being reported,” adds Wiener.

title: These 4 Celebs Are Already Confirmed for ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Season 35
summary: The cast of Season 35 of “Dancing With the Stars” will feature Maura Higgins, Ciara Miller, Jackson Olson and Guillermo Rodriguez.
story: The cast of Season 35 of “Dancing With the Stars” will soon sashay its way onto our screens.

A partial list of names who will compete for the covered Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy has trickled out in recent weeks. One star will follow in the footsteps of Robert Irwin, who won Season 34 of the show, along with pro partner Witney Carson.
“DWTS” returns with a two-night premiere that kicks off Sept. 15 and concludes the next night.
Here’s a look at who is confirmed to put their best feet forward on the upcoming edition of “DWTS.”
Maura Higgins
The “Love Island” and “Traitors” star is ready to show off her best moves.
“I’m a strong believer in manifesting. I had it on my vision board,” Higgins said about joining the show when her casting was announced at Hulu’s Get Real House event in April.
“And now it is happening, which I cannot believe, and I know it’s going to be so, so hard. But because I really want to do it, I’m going to put my all into it.”
Ciara Miller
The “Summer House” star, who appeared on a different season of “The Traitors” than Higgins, was also revealed to be a contestant during the April Hulu event.
“I am so excited to join Season 35 of ‘Dancing With the Stars.’ I feel like this is the perfect moment,” she said in a video message.

“I feel like I’m opening a new chapter, and I’m so excited to share it with all of you guys,” she said. “Can’t wait to put my energy on the dance floor, and Maura I can’t wait to share the dance floor with my fellow Faithful. See you soon.”
Jackson Olson
The Savannah Bananas star was announced as a contestant in May .
“I’m excited, but I’m also nervous,” he told E! News Aug. 20.

“The part I’m most excited for is I’ve only ever danced in cleats, on dirt and on grass. I can’t move my feet in a way that I can on a ballroom floor that I can on dirt and grass. It’s so tough on that baseball field to dance. But in that ballroom, I’ve become a different animal, I think, because it’s a three-hour rehearsal block. And I’m like, ‘Let’s go for three more hours.’ I want to get this down.”
Guillermo Rodriguez

It was revealed in June that the “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” sidekick will compete on the upcoming season. Earlier this week, it was announced that he will team with Carson, who is pregnant, sparking online chatter that the two were put together with the idea he will lose early, allowing her time to rest.
“Well, that’s not going to happen because I’m trying my best. I’m working hard, and I want to go all the way to the final,” he told guest host Rosie O’Donnell on “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” on Aug. 19.

title: Hayden Panettiere’s Ex Wladimir Klitschko Shares Emotional Post on Her 37th Birthday
summary: Hayden Panettiere’s ex-fiancé and father of their daughter, Wladimir Klitschko, has paid a touching tribute to the actor on social media on what would’ve been her 37th birthday.
story: Hayden Panettiere’s ex-fiancé and father of their daughter, Wladimir Klitschko, has paid a touching tribute to the actor on what would’ve been her 37th birthday.
The retired boxing legend posted a photo in remembrance of the late actor on Instagram Aug. 21, five days after the “Heroes” and “Nashville” star was pronounced dead in South Carolina.

“Today is Hayden’s birthday. Instead of celebrating the way we had planned, today we celebrate her life, her spirit, and the love she brought into this world,” he wrote. “I want to thank all of Hayden’s fans, friends, and everyone who has reached out for the incredible outpouring of love and support. At a time filled with so much sadness, your kindness has reminded me that there is still so much good in humanity.”
In his post, Klitschko also called on fans to spread love.
“If you’re reading this, I ask just one thing: even if only for a moment, think about LOVE,” he continued. “Reach out to a friend. Forgive someone. Be kind. Love is a superpower. Use it.
He concluded with a sweet message to Panettiere.
“Happy Birthday, Hayden. ❤️ You are loved, you are missed, and you will never be forgotten,” he wrote.
Klitschko is the father of the couple’s 11-year-old daughter, Kaya, and was engaged to Panettiere before they broke things off in 2018.
He previously shared an emotional message on Instagram two days after Panettiere’s death.
“To our daughter Kaya, I will always speak of her mother with respect and make sure she remembers the person she was,” Klitschko wrote.

Panettiere was found in cardiac arrest on Aug. 16 when emergency personnel responded to a 911 call at a residence where she had been temporarily staying in Greenville, South Carolina, according to a statement by the Greenville County Coroner’s Office. She was declared dead at 2:32 p.m. after EMS workers were unable to resuscitate her.
Dispatch audio from the emergency response references a possible overdose, but no cause or manner of death has been given by authorities.
The Drug Enforcement Agency has joined local authorities in the investigation into her death, a source familiar with the probe told NBC News on Aug. 20.

title: Asking Legendary Basketball Coach Geno Auriemma the Question He Asks Himself: Could He Do It All Again?
summary: Geno Auriemma reveals his thoughts about the new documentary “The Dynasty: UConn Huskies” and about being the winningest college basketball coach in history.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air.
Geno Auriemma had zero interest in coaching women’s basketball when he began coaching women’s basketball more than five decades ago.
“Who the hell would coach girls?” Auriemma snapped when a buddy asked him to be an assistant coach on a girls high school basketball team, before eventually agreeing, “Screw it, I’ll go.”
And there you have the origin story of the all-time most winningest coach in all of college basketball history.

Along with winning an unprecedented 12 NCAA championships, Auriemma has led the USA Basketball Women’s National Team to back-to-back Olympic gold medals in 2012 and 2016, respectively, has been inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame, the Women’s Basketball Hall of Fame, the FIBA Hall of Fame and, well, you get the drift.
Those are some pretty big shoes to fill, even for the guy who wears them, which is what Apple TV’s “The Dynasty: UConn Huskies” uncovers over the course of the three-part series, out Aug. 21.

The documentary also offers an unflinching, and sometimes unflattering, glimpse into what it takes to cultivate one of the biggest basketball dynasties in the world, starting with Auriemma’s fairy-tale success with the then small-town Huskies to the challenges of staying on top more than 30 years later.

Known for his larger-than-life personality, a quiet, introspective Auriemma speaks with TODAY.com in Studio 1A’s backstage Orange Room to unpack the documentary and what he reveals just might surprise you.
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.

Yes, I think there’s a lot of truth to that. No one, I don’t think, sets out to ... “Hey, I’m going to be a Hall of Fame writer,” or “Hey, I’m going to be a Hall of Fame coach, I’m going to be a Hall of Fame anything.”

They just start out, “I think I could be pretty good at this and let me see where it takes me.” Next thing you know, you look up and people are saying all these amazing things about you. And you do start to think, “Do you really deserve all that?” Because your part is not as big as the kids that were actually playing, scoring ... you know, doing.
The hardest thing I think ... I think of it that way, is — could you go back and do it again? And I don’t think I could. I don’t think I could.
I don’t know. Because it’s so improbable. If it wasn’t that unique, if it wasn’t that off-the-charts crazy, like, why hasn’t anybody else even come close to doing it?
That’s probably a good way to describe it. You do get hooked on the adrenaline of it it. You want that rush that comes from seeing something that you work so hard for come to fruition.

When you’re away from it, it’s really a relief to not have to deal with the pressure of having to perform at that level. But after you’re away from it a little bit, you kind of miss the being under the pressure, because the pressure makes you get up in the morning like, “Oh my God, I’ve got to do this today,” as opposed to, “What am I going to do today?”

That’s what we talk about. Or burst pipes. One or the other, you know? Either way, without it, it’s hard to achieve. We talk about that with the players. If there isn’t pressure to perform, if there isn’t a standard that you have to perform at, how will you ever know what your best is?

I think sometimes we’re afraid — and I find this today — we’re afraid to put ourselves out there because ... we only respect the outcome. And I do think that’s way different than it used to be. You’re an immediate success if do it right one time. And you’re an immediate failure if you fail one time. If you’re a young athlete, it’s hard to wrap your arms around that.

If I can think back clearly (to 1985), you really weren’t aware of how many people were paying attention, because they weren’t. So you were kind of doing it in a ... “Hey, I’m acting in a Shakespeare play in front of 100 people.” It’s not like I’m at Carnegie Hall, you know? I’m not on Broadway.
So you just take chances, you take risks and you’re not worried about, “What if this doesn’t work?”

Fast forward. Now, every little thing is scrutinized and I’m afraid that you lose some of that daring and some of that adventurous kind of, “Let me do it, I don’t care what people say.” It might be easy for me to say because I’ve been doing it for so long. But for a kid, it might not be so easy.

I think it has taken on a different meaning. But it’s kind of come full circle in the sense that you go back 35 years when we won our first championship and you go, “I did it. We did it. I did it. We did it. I did it.” And then, “You wanna do it again?” Because, otherwise, it was just a fluke.

And then it happens again. It’s like, “I did it. We did it. I did it. We did it.” I proved I could do it. Now, fast forward 40 years, and it’s like, “We don’t have to prove nothing. We don’t have to prove anything except that I can still do it.”

But, in between all those 40 years, you do start to realize, if you didn’t already, that it may be number 12 for you, but it was number one for all those kids on that team. So, you start to see like, “Man that’s how I felt when we won our first win.” Now, to be able to experience that with a group of kids, that’s pretty cool.
It’s almost like you’ve raised your kids and you were able to celebrate achievements. But now you’re doing it with your grandkids and, somehow or another, it just means more.

With grandkids, every time you walk in the room or they walk in the room, they remember, they jump on you, they can’t wait to see you. And they’re always happy when they see you because you’re not mad at them for what they didn’t do last night ... they didn’t do their homework, whatever, you’re not upset with them about anything.
And they just love being around you. Then, they go off and do their own thing. And now, I almost see my players as that. They come in, “Hey Coach! How are you doing?”
I think they want to be loved. They want to be appreciated. They want to be encouraged. They want to be told, “Hey, I think you’re pretty good.”
Whereas, 25 years ago, with Diana (Taurasi) and those guys, you’d go, “You suck at passing. Prove to me you’re a good passer.” (And they’d go), “I’ll show you.”
I don’t know if you can do that today. I think they get so much coming at them that if you say, “I think you suck at rebounding,” (they say), “Coach thinks I suck at rebounding.”
When you see some individuals, you know right away they’re different. Some, it’s a little more subtle. But for the best players we’ve ever had, you watch them play and you go ...

One of my former assistants had just gotten the job at UConn. We went out recruiting and she says, “I like that girl in the blue denim jacket. I like her.” And I went, “Hmm.” Then, go to another game and she goes, “That girl right there in the white. I like her.”
I went, “Hmm.”

And by the third or fourth game we watch, she goes, “The kid in the blue jacket. I really like her.” And I went, “Yeah.” And she says, “That’s a UConn player, huh?” I go, “Yeah. Do you see the difference now between the first two and that one?”
Once you see it, you go, “Yeah, yeah. That’s a Connecticut player.”

Then, when your team starts doing that in practice ... I remember when that great class graduated in 2002. The only one left was Diana (Taurasi). Sue (Bird), Tamika (Williams) Asjha (Jones), Swin (Cash), they all won the WNBA draft and Diana was the only one left. Now we come back to practice the following year and she’s a junior. The other four starters, two were freshman and two had never started a game ever at UConn.

So, she’s out there the previous year with four Olympians, and now she’s out there with two freshman and two other guys. And, like, the second week of practice, I looked over at one of our coaches and I said, “Goddamn, we’re going to be really good. I think we could be as good as last year.”
It was like (inhaling deeply), “Wow,” you know? Because you didn’t expect it. You thought, “Oh, this is going to be really hard, we’re going to have a lot of growing pains, bah, bah, bah.”
Because you’ve seen it so much (snaps his fingers), you know.
It’s like that comment about Vince Lombardi somebody once said, “A good coach knows when it looks right. A great coach knows when it is right.”

title: Who Is Chanty Beluga? Meet the Comedian Behind the Unforgettable Name
summary: Who is Chanty Beluga? What to know about the viral meme, created by comedian Courtney O’Donnell, of a woman introducing herself over and over again.
story: She’s going to a restaurant. She’s ordering takeout. She’s getting in an Uber.
In every instance, she makes sure to drop her name: Chanty Beluga.
Who is this smiling, millennial blonde woman whose videos have gone viral on TikTok? And where did that hypnotic and unique name come from?
Here’s what to know.
Who Is Chanty Beluga?
The character is the alter ego of comedian and actor Courtney O’Donnell, who posts TikTok videos of herself as Chanty Beluga.

Cheerful and demurely dressed, Chanty Beluga is always finding herself in situations where she has to use her goofy name. She’s checking in at a restaurant, ordering takeout, and introducing herself at a pool party.

The videos are quick and simple. Just a woman casually saying her ridiculous name, which seems to roll off the tongue and promote repeat listening. The character has already spawned multiple fan accounts on TikTok.

“This is so dumb and I see myself becoming rapidly obsessed with it,” one follower commented on a TikTok video of Chanty at a coffee shop. “No notes. Just a woman named Chanty Beluga in situations where she makes her name known.”
“Classic Chanty,” another one wrote.
“I would die for Chanty Beluga,” another commented.
Who Is Courtney O’Donnell, the Inventor of Chanty Beluga?

O’Donnell is a Los Angeles-based comedian who has a separate TikTok account under her real name. She posts short comedy skits as different, non-Chanty Beluga characters, from the host of the fictional “Yup, She Went There” podcast to a divorcée singing through the heartbreak.
She posted her first Chanty Beluga video on July 28 introducing herself, and it was a hit with nearly 500,000 views.

O’Donnell told Rolling Stone that she came up with the catchy name in the middle of the night while filming the upcoming comedy “Stephanie, Bride to Be” in Brooklyn, New York. She and the cast were “being silly” when it popped into her head.

“And I said, ‘Hi, my name’s Chanty,’ and we thought that was funny,” she said. “I was like, ‘Actually, my name is Chanty Beluga.’ We said the full name, and it seriously went viral in the room. We just could not stop saying Chanty Beluga. And I said, ‘Hi, my name’s Chanty,’ and we thought that was funny.”
Why Does the Internet Love Chanty Beluga?
The Chanty Beluga skits are so short, they allow O’Donnell’s followers to have fun by building out a longer story for the character.
“Chanty doesn’t play abt her takeout,” one follower commented on a video of Chanty Beluga ordering food.
“OMG IMAGINE BEING THE WORKER AND THE CHANTY BELUGA CALLS IN,” another joked.
The blank canvas of a character who’s not much beyond a funny name allows the internet to take it and run with it.

“She’s a Barbie doll. She’s a paper doll. You can put her in any situation. She can do anything,” O’Donnell told Rolling Stone. “I had this instinct to really build her up and create this crazy backstory, but I thought it was more interesting to allow the internet to create its own.”
Count Major League Baseball among those followers. The MLB X account posted on Aug. 18 that a woman named “Chanty Beluga” was presenting that day’s schedule of baseball games.

“Sometimes you go viral for something that you didn’t connect to, and I actually think this is really fun,” O’Donnell told USA Today. “I love pretending to be this woman on the internet who’s sort of quirky and basic and talking to people in the comments like I’m her.”
Then there’s one simple reason. Saying “Chanty Beluga” is fun.
“Something about the intonation of the words that feels like crack to say,” O’Donnell told Rolling Stone. “Something about the intonation of the words that feels like crack to say.”
Now the question is whether Chanty Beluga will reach the internet heights of 6-7 before people inevitably have had enough.

“I like the idea that she is the 6-7 for the girls and the gays,” O’Donnell told USA Today. “That would be really amazing. I don’t know. We’ll have to see. I’d be very happy. These things have a short shelf life, so I’m happy to just kind of be a part of it for now and let people have their fun. If we see some Halloween costumes, I won’t be mad.”

title: ‘I’m Not Hiding How Much This Hurts’: Malcolm-Jamal Warner’s Widow Honors His Birthday with an Emotional Message
summary: Malcolm-Jamal Warner’s widow honored the late “Cosby Show” star with a moving Instagram post on what would’ve been his 56th birthday on Aug. 18.
story: Malcolm-Jamal Warner’s widow honored the late “Cosby Show” star with a moving Instagram post on what would’ve been his 56th birthday on Aug. 18.
Tenisha Warner shared a picture of the couple’s 9-year-old daughter standing in a room filled with stuffed animals, while a “Happy Birthday” banner hung on a wall.

“Every year we spent his birthday at home, just the three of us,” Warner wrote. “He always said that was all he needed because it brought him the most joy to begin every new year of his life with us. The only other guests were our daughter’s dolls and stuffed animals. Every single one was lined up in the dining room to celebrate with him.
Warner also did not shy away from the agony she still feels about her husband’s death.
“Today is his birthday, and we are breaking as we try to learn how to be here without him,” she wrote.

“I’m not hiding how much this hurts. My gift to him includes my pain, because pain this deep only exists where love ran that deep. So today I’m sharing this with you who loved him too, the gift he gave us: he loved us with his whole heart, in ways I will never know again.”

Malcolm-Jamal Warner died July 2025 at the age of 54 in an accidental drowning while on vacation in Costa Rica with his wife and daughter. According to Costa Rica’s Judicial Investigation Agency (OIJ), he died as a result of asphyxia by submersion.

In September 2025, Tenisha Warner made her first public comments about her husband’s death as their anniversary approached while also announcing the creation of the charities River & Ember and The Warner Family Foundation in his honor.
“I can still hear my husband’s laugh, still feel the way he made room for every part of me — every tear, every dream,” she wrote, in part, on Instagram.
“Together we carry the legacy my husband and I began— one that nurtures children’s inner light and gives young artists the freedom to create outside the lines,” she added.

In July, Tenisha Warner sued Malcolm-Jamal Warner’s mother, Pamela Warner, for breach of contract involving the couple’s prenuptial agreement, which she claims they signed eight days before marrying in 2022. The lawsuit says the actor did not fulfill the obligations of the prenup, while Tenisha Warner claims that he “agreed to purchase and maintain a term life insurance policy on his life in the amount of $1,000,000,” with her as the “sole beneficiary.”

However, she says he never bought the life insurance policy for him or for her, even though they had an agreement. Her complaint also says the actor agreed to pay her $16,000 a year on their anniversary, create a retirement account and pay her a salary of $5,000 per month as his “chief of staff” but never did so.
The complaint claims that Tenisha Warner is owed “no less than $1,276,042.46,” plus interest and attorney’s fees and cost.
Pamela Warner has also publicly mourned his death.

“Malcolm was an exceptional husband, father, and son — a man deeply in love with life, his wife and his daughter,” she wrote in a statement posted on Instagram in August 2025. “He was not only my son, but also my teacher, coach, confidant, business partner, and best friend. He was the son that his father was immensely proud of and loved fiercely and unconditionally.”

TODAY.com has reached out to Pamela Warner for comment. According to a statement she shared with USA Today, a settlement has been reached. The statement said claims that Pamela sought to prevent her granddaughter from receiving financial support are untrue.

title: Bunnie XO Calls Life Post-Divorce a ‘Blessing,’ Shares She Wants to Have a Baby
summary: Bunnie XO opened up about her plans for having a baby during her TODAY interview.
story: Bunnie XO called her post-divorce life “a blessing” and reiterated that she still wants to have a baby after splitting from ex-husband Jelly Roll earlier this year.

The bestselling author and host of the hit “Dumb Blonde” podcast spoke on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle Aug. 20 about what her life is like since Jelly Roll, whose real name is Jason DeFord, filed for divorce on May 18, according to court records from Williamson County, Tennessee.
The split came two months before what would’ve been the couple’s 10th wedding anniversary.

“I know when something like that that’s deeply personal happens, it’s a beautifully tragic, but at the same time there’s always a silver lining, there’s always something better to look forward to,” Bunnie, whose real name is Alisa DeFord, told Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones. “There’s so much more to talk about with me especially, and with women, than their past lovers and people in their lives.”
On the June 18 episode of her “Dumb Blonde Podcast,” Bunnie XO confirmed the split. She also said it was “not mutual” and not her choice to break up.

She also revealed the surprising news that they still plan to have a baby together and would raise the child as co-parents. Jelly Roll has two children from previous relationships, daughter Bailee Ann, 18, and son Noah Buddy, 9.
Bunnie XO confirmed on TODAY that she still wants a child, but it was not clear if she wants the baby with her estranged husband.

“So I definitely still want to have a baby, and that’s going to be one of my newest chapters of my next book, and I can’t wait for you guys to read about it because it’s been one hell of a journey, let me tell you,” she said.

Bunnie XO and Jelly Roll have previously talked about their desire to have a child together. The couple announced in 2024 that they were trying to conceive through in vitro fertilization. Bunnie XO said on her June podcast episode that they had lost four embryos during their relationship together.
She also revealed on her podcast that Jelly Roll had started dating. In her interview on TODAY, Bunnie XO made it sound like she is also enjoying the single life herself.
“Ladies, they should’ve never let me back out in the streets because I love it here, and I’m never going back,” she said.

“I feel like us as women, we put ourselves aside so much for partners or friends, kids, and it’s like we don’t pour into ourselves, and sometimes you need to be selfish and you need to pour into yourself,” she continued. “And I just hope my journey can show people, ‘Hey, you know what, no matter how hard the situation you’re going through, you’re going get through that, you’re going to rise up, and you’re going to be an even better version of yourself.”
Jelly Roll cited irreconcilable differences as the reason for the split, according to the court filing. He and Bunnie XO each spoke out separately about the divorce filing.
Jenna and Sheinelle asked if Bunnie XO’s direct messages have been blowing up since the news of her divorce.
“I’m having the freaking time of my life,” she said. “I’m just thriving. I never thought it would turn out to be such a blessing, but it’s such a blessing, and I’m so thankful.”
She called her DMs “a freakin smorgasbord” of men and women.
“It’s so much fun in there, I don’t even know who to reply to,” she said. “It’s a lot. I love reading everbody’s DMs. Some of these pickup lines are amazing.”
Bunnie XO is also grateful if her perseverance through a difficult time in her personal life can help others.

“I’m not anybody’s role model, but if there’s something I can do that can encourage and inspire anybody along the way, then I hope that they get to take bits and pieces of my mistakes and my journey and apply it to their life,” she said.

title: Eli Rallo Reveals Cover, Excerpt from First Chapter of Her Debut Novel, ‘I Hope Eden Reads This’
summary: Eli Rallo reveals the cover and an excerpt from her debut novel, “I Hope Eden Reads This,” set to publish March 9, 2027.
story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a good story starts with a good first line. In TODAY’s “Cold Open,” authors tease their buzzy upcoming release by revealing and explaining its first line, paragraph or page.

Writing about 20-something female friendships and platonic “breakups” for her 2025 essay collection “Does Anyone Else Feel This Way?” influencer and podcaster Eli Rallo knew she had more to say on the topic.
But she needed to go deeper.

“I didn’t want to do it in a nonfiction vertical. I feel like I’ve said all I needed to say about my own personal experience or my own advice,” Rallo, who rose to online fame for doling out lifestyle “rules” for women navigating quarter-life, tells TODAY.com. “I don’t think I really necessarily have a ton of advice about how to navigate this.”
“I more so wanted to put words to it to make people feel less alone about it,” Rallo, 28, adds.

The result is her first novel, an exploration of the specific heartbreak that comes with dissolution of a decadeslong friendship, titled “I Hope Eden Reads This” — and TODAY.com has an exclusive first look.
After announcing her fiction debut to her cumulative one-and-a-half million social media followers in September 2025, Rallo officially unveiled its cover on Aug. 20.

The cover is an artistic portrait of two young girls, one with her eyes closed, another staring down the viewer. Rallo says she wants it to feel “so sad and tender” but also “emotional and intimate.” (While this cover was always her favorite, an alternative option was shaping up to be the winner from her publisher — until she got a “lovely, serendipitous” email on her birthday confirming the final.)
From the jump, Rallo says she knew the book needed to be blue.
“I felt like it had a Taylor Swift, ‘1989’ thing going on, like beachy blue vibes, New York City, all of that,” Rallo says.

“I Hope Eden Reads This” follows two childhood best friends, Penelope and Eden. Its premise establishes that the two, for whom “the term ‘best friend’ has never been enough,” are no longer speaking, and Penelope is falling apart. The book is told in dual timelines — one chronicling their friendship history, the other showing the aftermath of the breakup. The story is purposefully only told from Penelope’s perspective.

“I felt like the story had to be told from one side. It really is Penelope’s story, and Eden has a perspective in my mind and in my heart,” she says. “I’ve already received so much feedback from beta readers that people want to know more about what Eden was thinking, and I would rather leave them with that desire and maybe revisit it.”
So it’s fitting that the book’s first line of the first chapter starts with “I,” as Penelope reflects on the preteen years of her friendship with Eden:
I taught Eden how to kiss. I taught Eden how to do most things, if the definition of ‘taught’ is being brave enough to try things first and then report back my often-measly findings.

The book officially begins with a prologue, which Rallo says she wants keep a surprise for readers. So for TODAY.com’s “Cold Open” she shares the first few paragraphs of Chapter 1 (read the excerpt in full below).

She says this section was the very first thing she wrote about Eden and Penelope. Rallo wanted to channel “preteen awkwardness” and foreshadow an undercurrent of “toxicity” in intense female friendships that can go unnoticed — that is, until the relationship’s gone.

“When I look at the two characters, they have such an interesting relationship where they rely on each other for different things, and I think that their reliances on each other wind up becoming their demise in certain ways,” she says.

She says the book is generally inspired by friendship loss, but “what happens to these girls has never happened to me.” Rather both characters are a “patchwork quilt” of “every woman I’ve ever gotten to know or love,” she says. Excited to see whom readers will relate more with, she’s already prepared a Buzzfeed-style quiz to determine if you’re more of an Eden or more of a Penelope — and had to add an 11th question because she initially tied for both. (Rallo’s a Penelope, by one.)
When she first started to pitch the book, Rallo says people opened up to her about their own friendship losses, stories they seemed to have never been able to share before.
“It really felt like, at least to me, that everybody had an Eden. Whether they were ... 21 and an intern or 60 and a senior editor, everybody had an Eden story to share,” she says.
“I Hope Eden Reads This” is Rallo’s third book, joining her essay collection and 2023’s modern dating advice tome, “I Didn’t Know I Needed This.”

“I my whole life wanted to be a fiction writer,” she says. “I think my first two books were the only first two books I ever could have written. But I would be lying if I said that this didn’t feel like the biggest homecoming for me.”
Read the Beginning of ‘I Hope Eden Reads This’ Chapter 1

I taught Eden how to kiss. I taught Eden how to do most things, if the definition of ‘taught’ is being brave enough to try things first and then report back my often-measly findings. I was kissed first. So, I taught Eden how to kiss. This is mostly because I sought kissing out, and then kissing sought me out in return.

I was kissed for the first time 6 months prior, by a boy with red hair and one skinned knee, while we were sitting on the swings at the park across the street from our school, our feet turned toward each other. His name was Henry. We did not do tongue. I reported back to Eden. It was quick and maybe lasted 3 seconds? I tried to count how long it lasted while we kissed. Because what was the point of being kissed if not to report every moment, every detail to my best friend? I had to memorize the choreography of the whole thing. Deliver the information to her like a birthday gift, wrapped with a bow, sparing no detail.

I was kissing half because I wanted to and half because I wanted to share a new bit of knowledge with Eden. I craved filling that role. The bold teacher. That tenacious 13- year-old girl. Always the first to raise her hand. Always the first to try. The only thing Eden ever did first was get her period. She pulled me into the bathroom stall in 7th grade in the middle of lunch to tell me. We were 12. I faced her on the toilet. Read her the instructions on the back of a tampon box. I helped her put in a tampon for the first time though I had never done so myself. In every other way though, in any other scenario, I was first. Perhaps I was not better; I was hardly ever better. But I was always first.

title: ‘Saved By the Bell’ Turns 37: Watch TODAY Go Behind the Scenes of the Iconic Show in 1992
summary: “Saved by the Bell” executive producer Peter Engel talked to TODAY in 1992 about why the show was such a hit.
story: Welcome inside the TODAY Vault, where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment highlights the “Saved by the Bell” craze, and aired on July 24, 1992, by which time the show had cemented itself as a linchpin in NBC’s Saturday morning lineup.
On Saturday mornings in the 1990s, the alarm didn’t give out a warning, but teens knew they had to make it on time for one thing: “Saved by the Bell.”
The show, which premiered on Aug. 20, 1989, had become a full-blown phenomenon by the ‘90s, so much so that TODAY had to go to the set to see just what all the fuss was about.

The antics of Zack, Kelly, Slater, Jessie, Lisa and Screech have been well documented: The show helped redefine Saturday morning television and would lead to the short-lived primetime series “Saved by the Bell: The College Years,” as well as “Saved by the Bell: The New Class,” which followed and ran for seven seasons. “Saved by the Bell” is sacred to kids of the ‘90s, with a reboot released earlier this decade on Peacock.
‘Saved by the Bell’s’ Connection to TODAY
“Saved by the Bell” proved so influential, in fact, that it even had an impact on TODAY.
NBC decided to scrap Saturday morning cartoons altogether, adding other comedies like “California Dreams,” as well as a Saturday edition of TODAY in 1992.

Other live-action series, such as “Hang Time,” “City Guys,” “One World” and “Saved by the Bell: The New Class,” would eventually follow in the years to come in what would be known as NBC’s TNBC Saturday morning lineup.
Why Did ‘Saved by the Bell’ Shy Away From Serious Subject Matter?

“Saved by the Bell” executive producer Peter Engel said the show was “vilified” by critics for not being “on the cutting edge” by failing to address teen issues such as alcoholism, child abuse, divorce, sexual assault or teenage pregnancy.
“Those issues are very, very real and those problems are very, very prevalent, but not to the majority of teenagers,” he told TODAY.

“The majority of teenagers are not pregnant. The majority of teenagers are not having drinking problems. The majority of teenagers don’t have abusive parents,” he added. “We felt there were enough other shows in primetime dealing with these issues that we would deal with the issues that confront kids everyday.”

While the show did indeed have plots involving everything from aliens to a love detector, it didn’t completely shy away from serious subject matter: Fans will no doubt point to the classic episode in which Jessie gets hooked on caffeine pills, sparking perhaps the series’ most memorable line: “I’m so excited! I’m so excited! I’m so ... scared!”
What Made ‘Saved by the Bell’ a Hit?
The TODAY segment noted that the show was seen in 28 countries, dubbed into foreign languages. At the time, the cast was preparing to shoot a full-length movie for television.
“I’m convinced that one of the keys to success of this show is that our kids are playing their real ages,” Engel said. “They were really 14 playing 14, 15 playing 15, et cetera.”
